studyNotes.title: Module 01: Basic Engineering Drawing (Complete PSC Rank File Note)
studyNotes.description: Official Kerala PSC rank file notes on Drawing Instruments, Sheet sizes (IS 10711), Lines (IS 10714), Scales (Plain, Diagonal, Vernier), Conic sections, and 1st/3rd Angle Orthographic Projections.
chapterOverview: Drawing Instruments (Boards, T-squares, Set-squares, Pencils, Mini drafter)
Drawing Sheets (IS 10711: A0 to A5 sizes, aspect ratio √2:1, Title Block 185×65 mm)
Types of Lines (IS 10714: Types A to K) & Lettering Standards (IS 9609)
Scales: Representative Fraction, Plain, Diagonal, and Vernier (Least Count s/n)
Conic Sections: Ellipse (e<1), Parabola (e=1), Hyperbola (e>1), Cycloids, Involute
Orthographic Projections: First Angle vs Third Angle Projections, Points & Solids
takeaways: Trimmed size of A0 is 841 × 1189 mm (Area = 1 m²); A4 is 210 × 297 mm
Title block dimensions are strictly 185 mm × 65 mm at bottom right
BIS specifies First Angle Projection: Top view (Plan) is drawn BELOW the Front view (Elevation)

studyNotes.title: Module 02: Chain Surveying (Complete PSC Rank File Note)
studyNotes.description: Comprehensive study note on Principles of Surveying (Whole to Part), Metric & Gunter's chains, Tapes (Invar), Ranging, Slope corrections, Optical square, Obstacles, and Simpson's area rule.
chapterOverview: Fundamental Principles: Whole to Part & Point Location; Plane vs Geodetic Surveying
Chains & Tapes: Metric (20m/100 links, 30m/150 links), Gunter's (66 ft), Invar Tape (64% Steel, 36% Ni)
Ranging: Direct vs Reciprocal ranging; Slope stepping & Hypotensusal allowance (100(sec θ - 1))
Instruments for Right Angles: Optical Square (45° mirrors, 90° deflection), French Cross Staff
Errors & Tape Corrections: Erroneous length (L'/L), Temperature, Pull, Sag (-ve), Slope
Triangulation Framework (Base line, Check line, Tie line), Well-conditioned triangles & Simpson's Rule
takeaways: Working from whole to part prevents accumulation of local errors
Optical square operates on double reflection with mirrors at 45°
Sag correction is always subtractive (-ve); Invar tape has lowest thermal expansion

studyNotes.title: Module 03: Compass Surveying (Complete PSC Rank File Note)
studyNotes.description: Official lecture note on Prismatic vs Surveyor's Compass, Whole Circle Bearing (WCB) & Quadrantal Bearing (QB), Fore & Back Bearings, Magnetic Declination, Dip, and Local Attraction corrections.
chapterOverview: Meridians: True, Magnetic, Grid, Arbitrary; Convergence of Meridians
Prismatic Compass (0° at South, WCB, broad needle, prism) vs Surveyor's Compass (0° at N/S, QB)
Bearings: WCB to QB conversions, Fore Bearing & Back Bearing relation (BB = FB ± 180°)
Included Angles in Closed Polygon: Sum of interior angles = (2n - 4) × 90°
Magnetic Declination (TB = MB ± Dec), Dip (0° at equator, 90° at poles), Isogonic & Agonic lines
Local Attraction detection (|FB - BB| = 180°), Correction table, and Bowditch's Rule
takeaways: Prismatic compass graduated ring reads from South (0°) and is fixed to the needle
True bearing remains permanent over time; magnetic bearing varies with declination
At stations affected by local attraction, included angles between lines remain strictly correct

studyNotes.title: Module 04: Planetable Surveying (Complete PSC Rank File Note)
studyNotes.description: Official study note on Principle of Parallelism, Plane Table equipment (Alidade fiducial edge, Trough compass, U-fork), 4 methods (Radiation, Intersection, Traversing, Resection), and Lehmann's 3-point rules.
chapterOverview: Fundamental Principle of Plane Tabling: Parallelism; Field advantages & limitations
Equipment: Board, Tripod, Plain Alidade (Fiducial edge), Telescopic Alidade, Plumbing Fork & Plumb bob
Temporary Adjustments: Fixing, Leveling, Centering, Orientation (Back-sighting vs Magnetic needle)
Four Survey Methods: Radiation, Intersection (Graphic triangulation), Traversing, Resection
Two-Point Problem & Three-Point Problem (Tracing Paper, Bessel's graphical, Lehmann's trial method)
Lehmann's Three Rules, Danger Circle failure condition, and Centering vs Orientation errors
takeaways: Governing principle is Parallelism; no separate field book is kept
Back-sighting is the most accurate method of orientation; orientation error causes greatest displacement
Three-Point problem fails when occupied station lies on or near the Great / Danger Circle

studyNotes.title: Module 05: Levelling and Contouring (Complete PSC Rank File Note)
studyNotes.description: In-depth notes on Dumpy level, Sopwith staff, Height of Instrument vs Rise & Fall methods, Inverted staff readings, Reciprocal levelling, Curvature & Refraction (-0.0673d²), and Contour characteristics.
chapterOverview: Definitions: Level surface, Datum (MSL Mumbai High), Reduced Level (RL), Bench Marks (GTS, Permanent)
Instruments: Dumpy, Tilting, Auto Level (pendulum compensator), Sopwith Staff (5 mm least count)
Field Sights: Back Sight, Fore Sight, Intermediate Sight, Change Point; Two-Peg Collimation Test
Reduction of Levels: Height of Instrument vs Rise and Fall methods & Arithmetical check formulas
Inverted Staff Readings for bridge soffits & ceiling beams (recorded with negative sign)
Curvature (-0.0785d²), Refraction (+0.0112d²), Combined (-0.0673d²), Reciprocal levelling, and Contours
takeaways: Rise and Fall method provides full mathematical check on Intermediate Sights
Combined curvature and refraction correction: C = - 0.0673 d² (always subtractive)
Contour lines cross ridge and valley lines at 90°; never cross except in overhanging cliff

studyNotes.title: Module 06: Theodolite, Tacheometry & Curves (Complete PSC Rank File Note)
studyNotes.description: Transit Theodolite parts, least count 20", Face Left/Right, Latitudes & Departures, Closing error, Gale's table, Tacheometry (k=100, C=0, Porro's lens), Circular curves (R=1719/D), and Rankine's deflection method.
chapterOverview: Transit Theodolite: Designated by lower plate diameter; 5 fundamental axes; Least count = 20"
Adjustments & Angle Measurement: Spire test, Repetition vs Reiteration, Face Left & Face Right
Traversing: Latitude (l cos θ), Departure (l sin θ), Closing error e = √(ΣL² + ΣD²), Gale's table
Tacheometry: Stadia principle, Multiplying constant k=100, Additive constant C=0 (Anallatic lens)
Simple Circular Curves: Radius R, Tangent length T = R tan(Δ/2), Long chord C = 2R sin(Δ/2)
Setting Out Curves: Rankine's tangential angle method (δ = 1718.9 c / R min), Two-theodolite method
takeaways: Mean of Face Left and Face Right eliminates collimation error, horizontal axis tilt, and index error
Anallatic lens (convex lens by Porro) makes the additive constant exactly zero (C = 0)
Degree of curve for 30m arc: R = 1718.9 / D; for 20m arc: R = 1145.9 / D

studyNotes.title: Module 07: Modern Survey Instruments (Total Station, GPS & GIS)
studyNotes.description: Modern surveying technologies: Electronic Distance Measurement (Tellurometer, Distomat, Geodimeter), Total Station (REM, MLM, Stake-out), GNSS/GPS constellations, NavIC (IRNSS), RTK CORS network, and GIS.
chapterOverview: EDM Principles: Phase shift vs Pulse transit time; Microwave (Tellurometer), Infrared (Distomat)
Corner-Cube Retro-Reflector & Prism Constant (-30 mm or 0 mm)
Total Station: Dual-axis compensators, optical encoders, MLM, REM, Resection, PPM atmospheric correction
Global Navigation Satellite Systems: GPS (24 satellites, 6 planes), GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou
India's NavIC / IRNSS: 7 satellites (3 GEO + 4 GSO), 1,500 km regional coverage around India
Trilateration (min 4 satellites), DGPS, Real-Time Kinematic (RTK), Kerala CORS resurvey, Vector vs Raster GIS
takeaways: Total Station combines electronic theodolite + EDM + onboard microprocessor
Minimum 4 satellites needed to determine 3D position (X, Y, Z) and receiver clock bias (Δt)
Kerala falls primarily in UTM Zone 43 North (Zone 43N) with central meridian 75°E

studyNotes.title: Module 08: AutoCAD & CAD Commands (Complete PSC Rank File Note)
studyNotes.description: AutoCAD GUI, File extensions (.dwg, .dxf, .dwt, .bak), Coordinate systems (Absolute, Relative, Polar), Function keys (F1 to F12), Draw & Modify commands, OSNAP, Layers (Freeze vs Off, Defpoints), and Blocks.
chapterOverview: AutoCAD Interface: Application menu, Ribbon, Command line, Status bar, File formats (.dwg, .dxf, .dwt, .bak)
Coordinate Systems: WCS vs UCS; Absolute (X,Y), Relative Rectangular (@X,Y), Relative Polar (@D<A)
Drawing Setup: UNITS, LIMITS, ZOOM (All, Extents, Window), PAN, REGEN, VIEWRES
Draw Commands: Line, Polyline, Circle, Arc, Rectangle, Polygon (3-1024 sides), Ellipse, Hatch, Spline
Modify Commands: Move, Copy, Rotate, Scale, Offset, Trim, Extend, Fillet (R=0 sharp corner), Chamfer, Explode
Function Keys (F3 OSNAP, F8 Ortho, F10 Polar), Layers (Layer 0, Defpoints), Blocks (BLOCK vs WBLOCK)
takeaways: In AutoCAD default settings, 0° is East and angles are positive counter-clockwise
Fillet with Radius R = 0 creates a clean, sharp 90° corner between lines
Objects placed on Defpoints layer are visible on screen but NEVER plot on paper

studyNotes.title: Module 09: Workshop Calculation and Science (Complete PSC Rank File Note)
studyNotes.description: SI Units, Kerala land unit conversions (1 Acre = 100 Cents = 43,560 sq ft, 1 Cent = 435.6 sq ft), 2D/3D Mensuration, Prismoidal formula for earthwork, Mechanics, Horsepower (Metric 735.5W), and Trigonometry.
chapterOverview: Units & Measurements: SI base and derived units; Metric prefixes; Force (N), Work (J), Power (W)
Kerala Cadastral Conversions: 1 Cent = 435.6 sq ft = 40.47 m²; 1 Acre = 100 Cents = 43,560 sq ft; 1 Hectare = 10,000 m²
2D Mensuration: Triangles (Heron's formula), Quadrilaterals, Semi-circle perimeter = r(π+2) = (36/7)r, Ellipse
3D Mensuration: Volume & TSA of Cubes, Cylinders, Cones, Spheres, Hemispheres, Frustums
Earthwork Volumes: Prismoidal Formula (V = d/3 [A1+An+4Even+2Odd]), Prismoidal correction (-ve)
Mechanics & Machines: Density, Specific gravity, Equations of motion, HP (Metric 735.5W), Levers, Trigonometry
takeaways: 1 Acre = 100 Cents = 43,560 sq ft = 4,046.86 m²; 1 Cent = 435.6 sq ft = 40.47 m²
1 Metric Horsepower = 735.5 Watts; 1 British Horsepower = 746 Watts
Celsius and Fahrenheit thermometers read the exact same value at - 40° (- 40°C = - 40°F)

studyNotes.title: Module 10: Building Materials & Construction (KWA Tracer Master Note)
studyNotes.description: Building Stones, Bricks (Silica 50-60%, Alumina 20-30%, modular 190×90×90 mm), Cement (Bogue's compounds, setting times, soundness), Concrete grades (M20 RCC min), Masonry bonds, Irrigation (Δ=864B/D), and Highway geometry.
chapterOverview: Building Stones: Geological, Physical, Chemical rock types; Mohs hardness scale (1 Talc to 10 Diamond)
Bricks: Composition (Silica 50-60%, Alumina 20-30%), Modular size 190×90×90 mm, 500 bricks/m³, Compressive strength
Cement & Mortar: Bogue's compounds (C3S, C2S, C3A, C4AF), Setting times (≥30 min, ≤600 min), Soundness (≤10 mm)
Concrete: Abrams' law, Mix proportions (M15, M20, M25), Minimum grade for RCC = M20, Bulking of sand
Construction & Masonry: Rankine's foundation depth, English vs Flemish bond, Queen closer, King/Queen post trusses
Irrigation & Roads: Duty-Delta-Base period (Δ = 864B/D cm), Berms, Weirs vs Barrages, Camber, Superelevation e=v²/225R
takeaways: Modular brick size: 190 × 90 × 90 mm; 1 m³ brickwork requires exactly 500 modular bricks
Minimum grade of concrete for structural RCC under IS 456 is M20 (1 : 1.5 : 3)
Duty-Delta fundamental equation: Delta Δ = (864 × B) / D cm; English bond is strongest

pyqPapers.title: Kerala PSC Tradesman (Survey) / Surveyor Gr. II (Paper 063/2024)

questions.question: Which drawing sheet is most convenient for the class room drawing?
questions.explanation: A2 size (420 mm × 594 mm) is the standard and convenient drawing sheet size widely used in educational institutions and classroom drafting boards.

questions.question: Which pencil is used for construction lines, dimension lines, centre lines, section lines etc.?
questions.explanation: 2H pencil (hard grade) produces fine, crisp, and light lines ideal for construction lines, dimension lines, center lines, and section hatching.

questions.question: Which range of lettering is generally used for sub-titles and heading?
questions.explanation: As per Bureau of Indian Standards (IS 9609), lettering height of 3 mm to 6 mm is designated for headings, sub-titles, and section headers.

questions.question: Lines of hidden edges are drawn as :
questions.explanation: Dashed thin lines (Type E or F line as per IS 10714) are standard conventions for representing hidden outlines and hidden edges.

questions.question: In which system of dimensioning, all dimensions are placed from the bottom of the drawing sheet?
questions.explanation: In the unidirectional dimensioning system, all dimensions are oriented horizontally so they can be read solely from the bottom of the drawing sheet.

questions.question: In which the quadrilateral have only two sides are parallel and the four angles are different?
questions.explanation: A trapezium is a quadrilateral possessing only one pair of parallel sides with all four interior angles being unequal.

questions.question: When the section plane is inclined to the axis of the cone and is parallel to one of the generators the section is?
questions.explanation: When a cone is cut by a section plane inclined to its axis and parallel to one of its generators, the resulting conic section is a parabola.

questions.question: Which is the part of the circle or area bound by the arc and chord?
questions.explanation: A segment of a circle is the region enclosed between an arc and its corresponding chord. (A sector is enclosed by an arc and two radii).

questions.question: An actual length of 5 m of a room is represented by 25 mm length on drawing. Then Representative fraction of drawing is :
questions.explanation: Representative Fraction (RF) = Drawing Length / Actual Length = 25 mm / 5 m = 25 mm / 5000 mm = 1 / 200 (Scale 1:200).

questions.question: The elevation of a cylinder whose axis is parallel to VP and perpendicular to HP is :
questions.explanation: A cylinder with its axis parallel to VP and perpendicular to HP projects as a circle in the top view (plan) and a rectangle in the front view (elevation).

questions.question: What is the graphical representation of features on the earth surface or below the earth surface on a horizontal plane in a small scale is?
questions.explanation: A map (or plan) is the graphical representation to scale of natural and artificial surface or subsurface ground features. Small scale representations are maps; large scale are plans.

questions.question: Preliminary survey is used for :
options: Setting out the work on the ground
Determine the feasibility and rough cost of the scheme
Collecting more precious datas and choose the best location of the work and to estimate the quantities and cost
questions.explanation: A preliminary survey collects detailed spatial and topographical ground data to evaluate alternative routes, select the best alignment, and estimate quantities and cost.

questions.question: The limit of plane survey is :
questions.explanation: Plane surveying neglects the curvature of the earth and assumes the surface is flat for areas up to 250 km² (or 260 km²; 200 sq.km as per PSC official key).

questions.question: The main principle of survey is work from the whole to part for :
questions.explanation: The primary principle of surveying 'work from whole to part' localizes minor errors and prevents the cumulative expansion of measurement errors.

questions.question: Which tape is preferable for the highest precision work and used in measurement of base line to triangulation in the city work?
questions.explanation: Invar tape (36% Nickel, 64% Steel) has the lowest thermal expansion coefficient (1/10th of steel), making it ideal for base line and high-precision surveys.

questions.question: Which measurements are taken at right angles to the chain line of a survey work is?
questions.explanation: Perpendicular offsets are linear measurements taken at right angles (90°) to the survey chain line to fix lateral features.

questions.question: The limit of error in 30m Chain as per BIS :
questions.explanation: According to BIS standards, the permissible tolerance in the overall length of a 30 m metric chain under standard pull is ± 8 mm (± 5 mm for 20 m).

questions.question: The length of a line measured with a 20 m chain was to be 250 m. Calculate the true length of the line if the chain was 10 cm too long :
questions.explanation: True Length = (Measured Length) × (Actual Chain Length / Designated Length) = 250 m × (20.1 m / 20.0 m) = 251.25 m.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to reproduce plans to a different scale is?
questions.explanation: A pantograph is a drafting linkage instrument based on parallelogram mechanics used for enlarging, reducing, or copying plans to scale.

questions.question: A tape may be too long or an angle measuring instrument may be out of adjustment. Then such type of error comes under which source of error?
questions.explanation: Errors caused by a chain/tape being too long or an instrument being out of adjustment originate from the physical measuring tool itself (Instrumental error).

questions.question: In survey work the reciprocal ranging is applicable for :
options: When end stations are not inter visible
questions.explanation: Reciprocal ranging is employed when the two terminal survey stations are not intervisible due to an intervening hill, ridge, or high ground.

questions.question: The size of field book is :
questions.explanation: A standard field book used for recording survey chainage and offsets measures approximately 20 cm × 12 cm (200 mm × 120 mm).

questions.question: In sexagesimal system, 1 circumference =
questions.explanation: In the sexagesimal system of angular measurement, 1 complete circumference is divided into 360 degrees (360°), 1 degree into 60 minutes, and 1 minute into 60 seconds.

questions.question: __________ is any convenient direction towards a permanent mark or signal.
questions.explanation: An arbitrary meridian is any arbitrarily chosen convenient direction (such as a church spire, chimney, or permanent flagstaff) used as a reference line.

questions.question: The lines of force of earth’s magnetic field run generally from :
questions.explanation: Magnetic lines of force outside the earth generally emanate from the south magnetic pole and enter at the north magnetic pole (magnetic South to North).

questions.question: In surveyor’s compass the graduations are in :
questions.explanation: In a surveyor's compass, the graduated ring is divided into four quadrants from 0° to 90° at North and South to 90° at East and West (quadrantal system).

questions.question: The magnetic bearing of a line AB is S 28º 30’ E, calculate the true bearing if the declination is 7º 30’ W :
Convert the quadrantal bearing N 12º 24’ E to whole circle bearing :
questions.explanation: N 12° 24' E lies in the 1st quadrant (NE). In the whole circle bearing system, WCB = QB directly = 12° 24'.

questions.question: The fore bearing of a line AB is N 86º 12’ W find its back bearing :
questions.explanation: Fore Bearing = N 86° 12' W. In the quadrantal system, reverse the direction letters (N becomes S, W becomes E): S 86° 12' E.

questions.question: The bearing of a line AB is measured from A towards B, it is known as :
questions.explanation: The bearing of a line measured in the direction of the forward progress of the survey (from station A towards station B) is called the Fore Bearing (FB).

questions.question: The horizontal angle between the true meridian and the magnetic meridian is known as :
questions.explanation: Magnetic declination is the horizontal angle between the true (geographical) meridian and the magnetic meridian.

questions.question: The local attraction at a particular place can be detected by observing the _________ of each line and finding its difference.
questions.explanation: Local attraction at a station is detected if the numerical difference between the Fore Bearing and Back Bearing of a line is not exactly 180°.

questions.question: Inaccurate levelling of the compass box is a ___________ error.
questions.explanation: Failure to properly level the compass box by the surveyor is an error of manipulation caused by the observer (personal error).

questions.question: The extent of daily variations depend upon :
questions.explanation: Diurnal (daily) variation in magnetic declination depends upon the geographical locality, the season of the year, and the time of the day (All of these).

questions.question: ____________ is the process of determining the plotted position of the station occupied by the plane table, by means of sights taken towards known points, locations of which have been plotted.
questions.explanation: Resection is the plane table operation used to determine the plotted position of the occupied instrument station by sighting established control stations.

questions.question: The __________ is used to orienting the plane table to magnetic north.
questions.explanation: A trough compass is aligned along the edge of the plane table to establish and orient the board with respect to the magnetic north.

questions.question: Location of the position on the plan, of the station occupied by the plane table by means of observations to two well defined points whose positions have been previously plotted on the plan is known as :
questions.explanation: The two-point problem involves locating the plotted position of the station occupied by the plane table by sighting two known visible points.

questions.question: __________ is the process of putting the plane - table into some fixed direction so that line representing a certain direction on the plan is parallel to that direction on the ground.
questions.explanation: Orientation is the operation of keeping the plane table at successive stations parallel to its position at the first station.

questions.question: Methods of plane tabling can be divided into __________ distinct heads.
questions.explanation: Plane table survey methods are classified into four distinct heads: Radiation, Intersection, Traversing, and Resection.

questions.question: Which of the following is the permanent adjustment of dumpy level?
questions.explanation: The two-peg test is the permanent adjustment test of a dumpy level used to make the line of collimation parallel to the axis of the bubble tube.

questions.question: In contouring horizontal equivalent depends upon :
questions.explanation: Horizontal equivalent is the horizontal distance between two consecutive contour lines, which varies inversely with the steepness (slope) of the ground.

questions.question: Mean Sea Level (M.S.L.) is the average height of the sea for all stages of tides. It is the average of hourly tides for a long period of _________ years.
questions.explanation: Mean Sea Level (M.S.L.) is determined from hourly tidal observations averaged over a complete 19-year Metonic tidal cycle.

questions.question: What is the combined correction for curvature and refraction for a distance of 3 km?
questions.explanation: Combined correction: C_comb = 0.0673 × D² meters = 0.0673 × (3)² = 0.0673 × 9 = 0.6057 m ≈ 0.606 m.

questions.question: In the case of levelling across a river or lake, which type of levelling is used?
questions.explanation: Reciprocal levelling eliminates errors due to earth curvature, atmospheric refraction, and collimation error when sighting across wide rivers or ravines.

questions.question: In plotting the Longitudinal section (profile levelling), the vertical scale for showing the reduced level is enlarged to __________ times the horizontal scale.
questions.explanation: In profile levelling longitudinal sections, the vertical scale is enlarged 10 times compared to the horizontal scale to accentuate elevation differences.

questions.question: A set of V-shaped contours with higher value contours inside the bent represents a :
questions.explanation: V-shaped contour loops with higher contour values inside the loop represent a ridge line (watershed divide). (Lower values inside represent a valley/stream).

questions.question: What is the controlling factor for locating a highway or canal in a contour map?
questions.explanation: The ruling gradient (contour gradient) is the maximum permissible slope that governs the alignment of a road or canal in hilly terrain.

questions.question: What is the quantity of cutting given the ground level as 232.50 and formation level is 231.10?
questions.explanation: Depth of cutting = Ground Level - Formation Level = 232.50 m - 231.10 m = 1.40 m.

questions.question: When the sights are long _________ types of staff used for levelling work.
questions.explanation: When sights exceed 100-150 meters, a target staff with a movable target operated by the staff-man is used to avoid reading errors.

questions.question: Which surface is normal to the direction of gravity at all points?
questions.explanation: A level surface is curved and concentric with the mean shape of the earth, remaining normal (perpendicular) to the direction of gravity at all points. (Since 'Level surface' is not among A, B, C, 'None of these' is the official answer).

questions.question: Which level is that the line of sight remains horizontal once the operator has roughly levelled the instruments?
questions.explanation: An automatic level (auto level) incorporates an internal optical-mechanical pendulum compensator that automatically levels the line of sight.

questions.question: What is rise or fall, if back sight reading taken on B.M is 2.045 m and intermediate sight on point = 2.68 m?
questions.explanation: Rise / Fall = Back Sight (BS) - Intermediate Sight (IS) = 2.045 m - 2.680 m = -0.635 m. The negative sign represents a Fall of 0.635 m.

questions.question: Which instrument is used for establishing grade contour?
questions.explanation: An Abney level is a light, handheld instrument combining a sighting tube and spirit level used to measure slope angles and locate grade contours.

questions.question: In the formula for cross-sectional area of an embankment or cutting, A = Bd + Sd², what does 'S' represent ?
questions.explanation: In the cross-sectional earthwork area formula A = Bd + Sd² for an embankment or cutting, 'S' denotes the side slope ratio (S horizontal to 1 vertical).

questions.question: The latitude and departure of any point with reference to the preceding point are called :
questions.explanation: The latitude and departure of a survey station computed with respect to the immediately preceding station are termed consecutive coordinates.

questions.question: Which method of theodolite traversing, the magnetic bearing of only the first line is measured? The magnetic bearing of all other lines are determined indirectly:
questions.explanation: In the fast needle method of theodolite traversing, the magnetic bearing of only the initial line is observed; all other bearings are derived from measured angles.

questions.question: What are the fundamental lines of theodolite? (1) Horizontal axis (2) Line of collimation (3) Axis of telescope (4) Slant line
questions.explanation: The fundamental lines of a transit theodolite include: (1) Horizontal axis, (2) Line of collimation, and (3) Axis of telescope (along with plate level axis and vertical axis).

questions.question: What is the least count of stadia rod?
questions.explanation: A stadia levelling rod is graduated with bold patterns having a least count of 1 mm (0.001 m as designated in the official answer key).

questions.question: What is the distance from mid point of the curve to point of inter-section?
questions.explanation: The distance from the apex (Point of Intersection) to the midpoint of the curve is the apex distance (external distance): E = R [sec(∆/2) - 1].

questions.question: What is the formula for length of long chord of a simple circular curve?
questions.explanation: The length of the long chord connecting the two tangent points of a simple circular curve of radius R and deflection angle ∆ is given by L = 2R sin(∆/2).

questions.question: The axis about which the telescope and the vertical circle of the theodolite rotated in the vertical plane is called :
questions.explanation: The horizontal trunnion axis is the transverse axis about which the telescope and vertical circle rotate during vertical transit.

questions.question: What is the tacheometric equation for distance while the line of sight is horizontal and staff is held vertically?
questions.explanation: For horizontal sights with a tacheometer, the distance equation is D = (f/i)·s + (f + d) = k·s + c, where (f/i) is multiplying constant (100) and (f + d) is additive constant (0 for anallatic lens).

questions.question: Which method is suitable for closed traverse in theodolite survey?
questions.explanation: The included angle method is the most accurate and recommended method for theodolite traversing of a closed polygon.

questions.question: The component length measured perpendicular to the reference meridian is called :
questions.explanation: The component distance of a survey line measured perpendicular to the reference meridian (East-West direction) is termed its Departure (D = l sin θ).

questions.question: The DGPS technique is based on using atleast ___________ GPS receivers.
questions.explanation: Differential GPS (DGPS) requires at least two GPS receivers: one stationary reference base station at a known location and one roving receiver.

questions.question: In GPS survey, RTK stands for :
questions.explanation: RTK stands for Real Time Kinematic, a satellite navigation technique used to enhance the precision of position data in real time using carrier phase measurements.

questions.question: Which instrument is the combination of Electronic Theodolite and electronic distant meter?
questions.explanation: A Total Station integrates an electronic transit theodolite, an electronic distance meter (EDM), and an on-board microprocessor.

questions.question: The fundamental measurements with the Total Station are horizontal angle, vertical angle and :
questions.explanation: The primary raw measurements observed by a Total Station are horizontal angle, vertical angle, and slope distance. Horizontal and vertical distances are computed from these.

questions.question: Which projection uses the equidistant parallel lines for showing the meridians?
questions.explanation: A cylindrical projection (such as Mercator projection) represents meridians of longitude as equidistant parallel vertical straight lines.

questions.question: Which is the science of acquiring information about the earth’s surface without actually being in contact?
questions.explanation: Remote sensing is the science and technology of acquiring information about physical ground features without making direct physical contact using sensors on aircraft or satellites.

questions.question: Which is an Oceanographic device for flow of measurement?
questions.explanation: A current meter is an oceanographic and hydrometric instrument fitted with a revolving rotor used to measure the velocity of water flow in rivers and oceans.

questions.question: Which is the most accurate method of locating sounding?
options: Range and one angle from the shore
questions.explanation: Using a cross rope stretched across narrow rivers/channels is the most accurate method for locating hydrographic soundings.

questions.question: Which Line type is available when you start a new drawing in AutoCAD?
questions.explanation: In AutoCAD, the default linetype loaded automatically when initiating any new drawing template (acad.dwt) is 'Continuous'.

questions.question: Which command do you use to draw a circle in isometric drafting?
questions.explanation: In AutoCAD isometric drafting mode (Isometric Snap), circles on isoplanes are drawn using the ELLIPSE command with the 'Isocircle' option.

questions.question: To switch isoplane, you press :
questions.explanation: Pressing the F5 function key (or Ctrl + E) cycles through the three isometric planes: Isoplane Left, Isoplane Top, and Isoplane Right.

questions.question: ________________ command is used to restore all entities erased by the most recent Erase command.
questions.explanation: The 'OOPS' command in AutoCAD restores objects that were inadvertently deleted by the most recent ERASE command, even if other commands were run afterwards.

questions.question: Which is the short cut key of the text style?
questions.explanation: The command alias 'ST' (STYLE) opens the Text Style manager dialog box in AutoCAD.

questions.question: File, Edit, View etc. Are easily available in AutoCAD from?
questions.explanation: Standard drop-down menus (File, Edit, View, Insert, Format) are located on the AutoCAD Menu Bar at the top of the workspace.

questions.question: Which co-ordinate system is used in AutoCAD if we know the precise X and Y values in the point from the origin?
questions.explanation: The Absolute Coordinate System locates points by typing exact X,Y coordinates measured directly from the Cartesian origin (0,0).

questions.question: Which of the following software is limited for Auto CAD installation?
questions.explanation: Modern AutoCAD versions require 64-bit operating systems; Windows 10 is the officially supported baseline.

questions.question: Unit of heat in MKS :
questions.explanation: In the MKS technical system of units, the standard unit of heat energy is the Calorie / Kilocalorie (kcal), defined as heat required to raise 1 kg of water by 1°C.

questions.question: 1 Hectare = ____________ Are.
questions.explanation: 1 Hectare = 10,000 m². 1 Are = 100 m². Therefore, 1 Hectare = 10,000 / 100 = 100 Ares.

questions.question: Compute the value of 37.698 ÷ 1000 :
questions.explanation: Mathematical division: 37.698 ÷ 1000 = 0.037698.

questions.question: Melting point of Molybdenum is :
questions.explanation: Molybdenum (Mo) is a refractory metal with an extremely high melting point of 2,623°C (approx 2,620°C).

questions.question: 1 Newton = ____________ dyne.
questions.explanation: In the provisional answer key, (B) 10000 is given. Note: Physically 1 Newton = 10⁵ dynes (100,000 dynes) in standard CGS-SI conversion.

questions.question: 1 + tan² θ = ___________
questions.explanation: From fundamental trigonometric Pythagorean identities: 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ.

questions.question: Cot(90° + θ) = ___________
questions.explanation: From trigonometric co-function rules for angles in the second quadrant: cot(90° + θ) = -tan θ.

questions.question: Example for a third order lever :
questions.explanation: In a class 3 lever, the effort is applied between the fulcrum and the load. Examples include tweezers, human forearm, and forceps.

questions.question: The property of a metal to resist the effect of tensile forces :
questions.explanation: Tenacity (tensile strength) is the mechanical property of a material that enables it to withstand pulling or stretching forces without breaking.

questions.question: The type of caste iron which cannot be welded :
questions.explanation: White cast iron contains carbon in the form of cementite (iron carbide, Fe3C); it is extremely hard, brittle, and practically un-weldable.

questions.question: Density of water in gm/cm³ [as given in paper] :
questions.explanation: In the provisional answer key, (B) 1000 is given (which corresponds to 1000 kg/m³ in standard SI units; in CGS units pure water density is 1.0 gm/cm³).

questions.question: What will be the velocity of the body, when the body travels a distance of 180 m in a straight line in 20 seconds?
questions.explanation: Velocity = Distance / Time = 180 m / 20 s = 9 m/sec.

questions.question: Which is the most powerful neutral refractory material?
questions.explanation: Chromite (chrome brick) is chemically neutral, highly resistant to acidic and basic slag, and considered the most powerful neutral refractory.

questions.question: The Lime containing more than 30% of clay is known as :
questions.explanation: Poor lime (lean lime) contains more than 30% clay and impurities, slakes very slowly, and forms a thin mortar used for inferior work.

questions.question: Well grade sand should be pass BIS no.480 and should not pass BIS No. _____________ sieve.
questions.explanation: Well-graded aggregate sand for mortar/concrete passes BIS sieve No. 480 (4.75 mm) and is completely retained on BIS sieve No. 15 (0.15 mm / 150 micron).

questions.question: Wood absorbing water vapours from air is known as :
questions.explanation: Hygroscopicity is the property of timber and porous materials by which they absorb moisture/water vapor directly from the surrounding atmosphere.

questions.question: What is the name of first watering given to a crop, when the crop is a few centimeter height?
questions.explanation: Kor watering is the deep watering applied to agricultural crops when the young plants are a few centimeters high.

questions.question: Road constructed to secure access from a road to a private property is known as :
questions.explanation: A driveway is a private road or access lane providing vehicular access from a public highway to an adjacent private property or garage.

questions.question: The permissible gradient in the alignment of highway is known as :
questions.explanation: Ruling gradient is the maximum design gradient permissible along a highway alignment that vehicles can negotiate with normal power.

questions.question: How much percentage of Centage is added in estimate?
questions.explanation: Centage charges (departmental overhead charges) ranging from 10% to 15% are added to preliminary estimates to cover engineering establishment, supervision, and design.

pyqPapers.title: Kerala Water Authority (KWA) Surveyor Grade II (Paper 106/2017)

questions.question: ___________ is the equation for finding correction value for refraction.
questions.explanation: Atmospheric refraction bends the line of sight downward toward the earth, giving a correction of C_r = +0.0112 D² meters (where D is distance in km).

questions.question: Slope along the longitudinal direction is often termed as
questions.explanation: The rate of rise or fall of the ground surface along the longitudinal direction of a road, canal, or railway is termed the gradient.

questions.question: Level reading taken on a BM is 2.000. RL of BM is 10.000. Then a level reading of 3.500 was taken on top of a stake. Find the RL of the top of the stake:
questions.explanation: Height of Instrument (HI) = RL of BM + Staff Reading on BM = 10.000 + 2.000 = 12.000 m. RL of Stake = HI - Reading on Stake = 12.000 - 3.500 = 8.500 m.

questions.question: Equal gradient lines along a slope are called
questions.explanation: A grade contour is a line on the ground along which a constant uniform slope (gradient) is maintained.

questions.question: The latitude and departure with reference to preceding point are known as _____
questions.explanation: Consecutive coordinates (latitude and departure) of a station are computed with reference to the immediately preceding traverse station.

questions.question: What is the type of angle useful for alignment of highways, railways, canals etc?
questions.explanation: Deflection angles (angle between prolongation of preceding line and forward line) are extensively used for route surveying of highways, railways, and canals.

questions.question: What is the test carried in theodolite to make the horizontal axis perpendicular to the vertical axis?
questions.explanation: The Spire test (horizontal axis test) is performed to ensure that the horizontal trunnion axis is perpendicular to the vertical axis of the theodolite.

questions.question: When the angular measurements are more precise than the linear measurements, balancing the traverse is done by
questions.explanation: The Transit rule is applied to adjust traverse misclosure when angular measurements are more precise than linear measurements.

questions.question: The chord between two successive regular stations on a curve is known as _____
questions.explanation: In curve layout, a normal chord is the full standard chord between two consecutive full chainage peg stations on a circular curve.

questions.question: What is the multiplying constant, if adopting anallatic lens in the telescope of a tacheometer?
questions.explanation: An anallatic lens placed between the objective and eyepiece eliminates the additive constant (f + d = 0), leaving the multiplying constant k = f/i = 100.

questions.question: What is the distance between point of intersection to point of tangency?
questions.explanation: Tangent distance is the straight distance measured from the Point of Intersection (V) to either Point of Tangency (T1 or T2): T = R tan(∆/2).

questions.question: Which curve is generally introduced on highway between a straight and circular curve to provide ease and gradual change of direction?
questions.explanation: A transition curve (clothoid / spiral) provides a gradual transition from zero curvature on a tangent to the finite radius of a circular curve, preventing sudden centrifugal jerks.

questions.question: Which method is used for short traverse in theodolite survey?
questions.explanation: The fast needle method is used for running short traverse lines using the theodolite's compass without individual vernier angle computations.

questions.question: What is the multiplying constant in tacheometric survey?
questions.explanation: In tacheometry, the multiplying constant is given by the focal length divided by stadia hair interval: k = f / i (normally designed as 100).

questions.question: The fine adjustment in theodolite is done by
questions.explanation: In a theodolite, after clamping the motion screw, fine adjustment and precision sighting of the crosshairs is made using the tangent (slow-motion) screw.

questions.question: The face left position is also called
questions.explanation: Telescope normal (or face left) describes the position where the vertical circle is situated to the observer's left when looking through the eyepiece.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a traversing method?
questions.explanation: Open traversing is a geometric classification of traverse paths (unclosed), whereas chain, compass, theodolite, and plane table traversing are instrument methods.

questions.question: The telescope is rotated in horizontal plane relative to which axis?
questions.explanation: The telescope of a theodolite rotates in a horizontal plane about its vertical axis. Note: in official PSC provisional key Trunnion axis is given as (C).

questions.question: Imaginary line joining centre of the eyepiece and the objective of the telescope is
questions.explanation: The imaginary line connecting the optical center of the objective lens and the center of the eyepiece is the optical axis of the telescope.

questions.question: Horizontal angle as well as vertical angle can be measured using a
questions.explanation: A transit theodolite is designed to measure both horizontal and vertical angles with high precision.

questions.question: Point where the circular curve begins is called as
questions.explanation: The Point of Curve (P.C.) is the tangent-curve junction where the circular curve begins. Point of Tangency (P.T.) is where it ends.

questions.question: Projection of a survey line onto N-S line is termed as
questions.explanation: The projection of a traverse survey line onto the North-South reference meridian is called its Latitude (L = l cos θ).

questions.question: Which of the following is known as the ideal transition curve ?
questions.explanation: An ideal transition curve has a rate of change of radial acceleration that is uniform; the clothoid (Euler spiral) meets this condition with curvature increasing linearly with length.

questions.question: Process of revolving telescope of theodolite in the horizontal plane with respect to vertical axis of the theodolite is called
questions.explanation: Swinging the theodolite is the operation of rotating the telescope about the vertical axis in a horizontal plane.

questions.question: Angle subtended by radius at the centre of the curve is called as
questions.explanation: The angle subtended at the center of a circular curve by the arc connecting two tangent points is called the central angle (equal to the total deflection angle ∆).

questions.question: Angle between the preceding line and succeeding line is called
questions.explanation: The deflection angle is the angle between the prolongation of the preceding survey line and the forward succeeding survey line.

questions.question: The multiplying constant of a tacheometer fitted with an anallactic lens is
questions.explanation: The multiplying constant of a tacheometer equipped with an anallatic lens is k = f/i = 100.

questions.question: Which of the following is called as Easement curve ?
questions.explanation: An easement curve is another engineering term for a transition curve, easing the change in curvature and super-elevation between tangents and circular arcs.

questions.question: Two straights connected using a single arc of constant radius is known as
questions.explanation: A simple circular curve consists of a single arc of constant radius connecting two intersecting straight tangents.

questions.question: In India a curve is designated by
questions.explanation: In Indian railway and highway engineering practice, curves are designated by their degree of curvature (D) subtended by a standard 30 m or 20 m chord.

questions.question: Which of the following is also referred as versed sine of the curve ?
questions.explanation: The versed sine of a curve is the mid-ordinate (M), which is the perpendicular distance from the center of the long chord to the apex of the curve.

questions.question: Which of the permanent adjustment test checks the perpendicularity between horizontal axis and vertical axis ?
questions.explanation: The Spire test checks and adjusts the horizontal trunnion axis to be perpendicular to the vertical axis of the theodolite.

questions.question: The most widely used antenna in GPS is
questions.explanation: Microstrip patch antennas are the most widely used compact GPS antennas due to their low profile, light weight, and circular polarization capability.

questions.question: The first GPS satellite was launched in
questions.explanation: The first prototype GPS Block I satellite (Navstar 1) was launched into orbit on February 22, 1978.

questions.question: Which type of wave is used to operate EDM?
questions.explanation: Electronic Distance Measurement (EDM) devices transmit modulated electromagnetic waves (infrared, visible laser, or microwave) to measure distances.

questions.question: Data collector is used for total station?
questions.explanation: In Total Station surveying, the internal electronic data collector records slope distances, horizontal and vertical angles, and point coordinates in digital storage.

questions.question: An EDM based instrument is
questions.explanation: A Total Station is an integrated electronic instrument combining an electronic theodolite, an EDM, and a microprocessor data collector.

questions.question: Expand GPS
questions.explanation: GPS stands for Global Positioning System, a satellite-based radionavigation system developed by the United States Department of Defense.

questions.question: Which year does first microprocessor was invented?
questions.explanation: The world's first single-chip commercial microprocessor, the Intel 4004 (4-bit CPU), was invented and released in 1971 by Federico Faggin, Ted Hoff, and Stanley Mazor.

questions.question: What is the full form of GUI?
questions.explanation: GUI stands for Graphical User Interface, enabling users to interact with software through visual icons. (In official answer key, option D Geometrical user interface was marked).

questions.question: What is the use of function key F3?
questions.explanation: In AutoCAD drafting, the F3 function key toggles Running Object Snap (OSNAP) on and off.

questions.question: Which of the following software is limited for AutoCAD installation?
questions.explanation: AutoCAD compatibility has evolved; Windows 10 is the supported 64-bit platform while legacy systems are limited/unsupported.

questions.question: What is the use of the short cut key M text?
questions.explanation: In AutoCAD, the command alias 'MTEXT' (or MT) invokes Multiline Text creation.

questions.question: What is the full form of UCS?
questions.explanation: UCS stands for User Coordinate System, allowing drafters to orient X, Y, and Z axes relative to any workplane.

questions.question: Which of the following pointing device is cheaper while comparing the digitilizer?
questions.explanation: A computer mouse is an inexpensive, ubiquitous pointing device compared to an electromagnetic digitizer tablet/puck.

questions.question: Which short cut key does the work of redo last action?
questions.explanation: The standard keyboard shortcut to Redo the last undone action in Windows/AutoCAD is Ctrl + Y (while Ctrl + Z is Undo).

questions.question: Of the following which is the correct input method to draw a line of 100 units at an angle of 40° in anticlockwise direction from positive X axis on a default AutoCAD working space ?
questions.explanation: In AutoCAD, polar coordinates are input as @distance<angle, so 100 units at 40° anticlockwise from positive X is input as @100<40.

questions.question: Which function key is used for on/off object snap, while drafting in AutoCAD ?
questions.explanation: In AutoCAD drafting, the F3 function key toggles Running Object Snap (OSNAP) mode on and off.

questions.question: The path tracked by a projectile is called
questions.explanation: The parabolic path described by a projectile moving under the action of gravity in the absence of air resistance is termed its trajectory.

questions.question: Π Radians = ___________ grades
questions.explanation: In the centesimal angle measurement system, 1 right angle = 100 grades (100g). Thus, π radians (180°) = 200 grades.

questions.question: What is termed as the quantity of matter contained in a body?
questions.explanation: Mass is the fundamental scalar quantity of matter contained in a body, which remains invariant regardless of gravitational field.

questions.question: How many watts for 1 horse power in British system?
questions.explanation: In the British Imperial engineering system, 1 mechanical horsepower (hp) equals 746 Watts (550 ft·lbf/s). Metric hp equals 735.5 W.

questions.question: What is the S.I. unit of heat?
questions.explanation: In the International System of Units (SI), heat energy is measured in Joules (J). Note: In official provisional answer key, Option A Calorie is recorded.

questions.question: What is called for the materials that restricts heat flow by radiation, conduction and convection?
questions.explanation: Thermal insulators are materials with very low thermal conductivity that resist the transfer of heat by conduction, convection, and radiation.

questions.question: What is the term for the object seen higher than eye level?
questions.explanation: The angle subtended between the horizontal line of sight and the inclined line directed to an object above eye level is the angle of elevation.

questions.question: What is the centre of gravity of a sphere?
questions.explanation: By spherical symmetry, the center of gravity of a uniform solid sphere lies exactly at its geometric center.

questions.question: What is the purpose of tempering a steel?
questions.explanation: Tempering is a heat treatment process performed after hardening to reduce excessive brittleness and relieve internal quenching stresses while maintaining toughness.

questions.question: What is the term used for maximum stress attained by a material before rupture?
questions.explanation: Ultimate stress (tensile strength) is the maximum nominal stress attained on the engineering stress-strain curve prior to necking and rupture.

questions.question: Which formula is suitable for the area of a circle, whose diameter is (d)?
questions.explanation: The area of a circle in terms of its diameter d is Area = π (d/2)² = π d² / 4.

questions.question: What is the area of irregular shape by Simpson's rule?
questions.explanation: Simpson's 1/3rd rule for computing area under an odd number of ordinates (even number of intervals h) is Area = (h/3) × [(y1 + yn) + 4(sum of even) + 2(sum of odd)].

questions.question: What are the three consecutive numbers if their sum is 42?
questions.explanation: Let three consecutive integers be x, x+1, x+2. Their sum 3x + 3 = 42 => 3x = 39 => x = 13. The numbers are 13, 14, 15.

questions.question: What is the value of (a⁵)⁷ ?
questions.explanation: According to the laws of exponents, (a^m)^n = a^(m × n). Thus, (a⁵)⁷ = a^(5 × 7) = a³⁵.

questions.question: 1 m = __________ cm.
questions.explanation: In the metric system, 1 meter = 100 centimeters = 1000 millimeters.

questions.question: 1 hectare = ___________ m².
questions.explanation: 1 hectare = 100 m × 100 m = 10,000 m² = 10⁴ m².

questions.question: 6020 seconds =
questions.explanation: 6020 seconds / 60 = 100 minutes and 20 seconds. 100 minutes = 1 degree and 40 minutes. Thus, 6020" = 01° 40' 20".

questions.question: Formula for finding area of a plane triangle whose base is b, height h, is:
questions.explanation: The geometric area of a plane triangle with base b and vertical altitude h is Area = 0.5 × base × height = 0.5 bh.

questions.question: What is the abbreviation for MOEF?
questions.explanation: MOEF stands for Ministry of Environment and Forests (now MoEFCC: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change).

questions.question: What is the other name of dwelling unit?
questions.explanation: A dwelling unit is defined in building bye-laws and the National Building Code (NBC) as a residential building or apartment.

questions.question: What is the normal life period of residential building with concrete roof according to NBC 2005?
questions.explanation: According to NBC 2005 / IS 456, the design life period for monumental and permanent residential buildings with reinforced concrete roofs is 100 years.

questions.question: The standard size of brick
questions.explanation: The standard modular size of a common building brick as per BIS IS 1077 is 19 cm × 9 cm × 9 cm (nominal size with mortar is 20 × 10 × 10 cm).

questions.question: The central part of the tree is called
questions.explanation: The innermost core/central portion of a tree stem is the pith (or medulla), which supplies nutrients to young saplings.

questions.question: Weight of 1 bag of cement
questions.explanation: As per Indian Standard IS 1489 / IS 269, a standard commercial bag of Portland cement weighs exactly 50 kg (volume ≈ 34.7 liters).

questions.question: Chemically which rock is calcarious rock?
questions.explanation: Marble is a metamorphic rock formed from recrystallized limestone/dolomite, whose primary chemical constituent is calcium carbonate (calcarious rock).

questions.question: Vicat's apparatus is used to determine the
questions.explanation: Vicat's apparatus with standard plunger and needles is used to determine the standard consistency, initial setting time, and final setting time of cement paste.

questions.question: The structure which is used to carry canal over natural drain is called
questions.explanation: An aqueduct is a cross-drainage structure in which the irrigation canal is carried in a flume supported on piers completely over a natural stream/drain.

questions.question: Area of land irrigated divided by the unit volume of irrigation water is called
questions.explanation: Duty is defined as the area of land (in hectares) that can be irrigated by a continuous discharge of 1 cumec of water throughout the base period.

questions.question: Portion of a brick made by cutting across it lengthwise into exactly two parts is known as
questions.explanation: A queen closer is formed by cutting a standard brick lengthwise into two equal halves.

questions.question: When the bed level of canal and drainage is at the same level, is provided.
questions.explanation: When the bed levels of a canal and a natural drainage stream intersect at the exact same level, a level crossing with regulator gates is provided.

questions.question: Main constituent of portland cement is
questions.explanation: Lime (calcium oxide, CaO, 60-67%) is the primary chemical constituent of Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC), followed by silica (17-25%).

questions.question: In , headers and stretchers are laid alternatively in the same course.
questions.explanation: In a Flemish bond, alternate stretchers and headers are laid in the same course, with queen closers placed next to quoin headers in alternating courses.

pyqPapers.title: Kerala PSC Tracer / Surveyor Grade II (Paper 43/2023)

questions.question: As per BIS (IS 1444-1989) the standard size of B1 drawing board is _________
questions.explanation: Standard drawing board sizes as per BIS (IS 1444-1989): B0 = 1000 × 1500 mm, B1 = 700 × 1000 mm, B2 = 500 × 700 mm, B3 = 350 × 500 mm.

questions.question: For drawing long thin lines of uniform thickness the pencil should be sharpened
questions.explanation: A chisel edge is sharpened to maintain a uniform line thickness along straight edges (ruler/T-square). Conical points wear rapidly and broaden line width.

questions.question: The ratio of length to width of all arrow heads in drawing is
questions.explanation: According to SP 46 / IS 10714 drafting standards, dimension arrowheads must have a standard length-to-width (depth-to-spread) ratio of 3:1.

questions.question: For thin chain line alternate long and short dashes are in proportion ranging from
questions.explanation: For thin chain lines (center lines / Type G), long dashes are 9 to 12 mm and short dashes are 1.5 to 2 mm, giving a proportion ranging from 6:1 to 4:1.

questions.question: The plan and elevation of a line segment are seen coincides, the line is situated in the
questions.explanation: When a line lies in the 2nd quadrant (above HP, behind VP) or 4th quadrant (below HP, in front of VP), upon rotating HP by 90°, the plan (top view) and elevation (front view) overlap on the same side of the reference line XY.

questions.question: The recommended dimensioning of a sphere of Diameter 20 mm is
questions.explanation: As per ISO/BIS drafting conventions, spherical diameter is dimensioned by prefixing the symbol 'S' before the diameter symbol Ø, formatted as S Ø 20 (or SR for spherical radius).

questions.question: The type of Vernier in which the Vernier divisions are marked in the opposite direction of the main scale is
questions.explanation: In a backward (retrograde) vernier, divisions are numbered in the direction opposite to the main scale, where n vernier divisions equal (n + 1) main scale divisions.

questions.question: The method of projection in which the projectors are parallel to each other and perpendicular to the plane the projection is
questions.explanation: Orthographic projection is an axonometric/parallel projection method where projection rays are mutually parallel to each other and normal (perpendicular) to the projection plane.

questions.question: RF = 200:1 represents a
questions.explanation: Representative Fraction (RF) > 1 (e.g. 200:1) indicates an enlarging scale used for small precision components. RF < 1 is a reducing scale.

questions.question: Scale 1 : 200 is classified as
questions.explanation: A scale of 1:200 has an RF < 1, meaning 1 unit on the drawing represents 200 units in reality; it is a reducing scale.

questions.question: The survey in which earth's curvature is taken into account is
questions.explanation: In geodetic surveying, the curvature of the earth's spheroidal surface is taken into account for large areas (> 250 km²).

questions.question: Surveying Chain is Made up of
questions.explanation: Survey chains are manufactured from galvanized mild steel (MS) wire of 4 mm diameter (8 SWG) with ends looped into rings.

questions.question: The Length of surveyor's chain is
questions.explanation: Gunter's chain (surveyor's chain) is 66 feet (20.12 m) long and consists of 100 links, with each link measuring 0.66 ft (7.92 inches).

questions.question: In ordinary chain survey the maximum permissible error is
questions.explanation: In ordinary chain surveying under normal field conditions, the maximum permissible ratio of error is 1 in 1000 (1 in 250 in rough ground; 1 in 1000 is official key for standard ordinary chaining).

questions.question: The correction for sag is always _____
questions.explanation: Correction for sag is always negative (-ve) because the catenary curve makes the measured distance between supports longer than the true straight chord distance.

questions.question: If L is the correct length of a chain, L' is the incorrect length and D' is the measured length, then the correct length is:
questions.explanation: True distance = (Measured length) × (Incorrect length of chain / True length of chain) = D' × (L' / L).

questions.question: The instrument which is not used in chain survey is
questions.explanation: A levelling staff is used exclusively in levelling and tachometric work to measure vertical elevations, not for linear distance measurement in chain surveying.

questions.question: The Principle of chain surveying is
questions.explanation: The fundamental principle of chain surveying is triangulation, whereby the survey area is partitioned into a network of well-conditioned triangles.

questions.question: The system of lines or Triangles covering the area to be surveyed is
questions.explanation: The system of survey lines forming the skeleton network of triangles covering the area to be surveyed is called the framework.

questions.question: In a well-conditioned triangle the angles are
questions.explanation: A well-conditioned triangle has no angle less than 30° and no angle greater than 120° to minimize geometric plotting distortion.

questions.question: The line joining some fixed points termed as tie stations on main survey line is called
questions.explanation: A tie line joins auxiliary (tie) stations on main survey lines to measure offsets for locating interior ground details.

questions.question: Invar tape is made up of an alloy of and steel.
questions.explanation: Invar is a nickel-iron alloy (36% Nickel, 64% Steel) characterized by an exceptionally low coefficient of thermal expansion.

questions.question: The process of establishing an intermediate point in a line is called
questions.explanation: Ranging is the operational process of aligning intermediate points along a straight survey line between two terminal stations.

questions.question: Error =
options: Difference in values and sign of observed value
Difference in values and sign of true value
questions.explanation: By standard definition, Error = Observed Value - True Value (while Correction = True Value - Observed Value = -Error).

questions.question: Of the following, which is the primary stage of surveying ?
questions.explanation: Reconnaissance is the initial ground inspection of the survey area to observe boundaries, terrain features, and select station points.

questions.question: Bad ranging is an example for
questions.explanation: Bad (imperfect) ranging causes the chain to deviate from a true straight line, consistently making the measured length greater than the true length (positive cumulative error).

questions.question: Survey lines set out to locate interior details of a plot is called
questions.explanation: Tie lines are secondary lines run across main survey lines to locate interior ground features and details.

questions.question: A link of a metric chain is cm in length.
questions.explanation: Each link of a standard 20 m or 30 m metric chain measures 0.2 m (20 cm) between the centers of connecting rings.

questions.question: Which of the following is the prime instrument is used for ranging ?
questions.explanation: Ranging rods (typically 2 to 3 m long, octagonal or circular poles painted in alternating red/black and white bands) are the prime tools for visual alignment.

questions.question: A 20 m metric chain has links.
questions.explanation: A 20-meter metric chain consists of 100 links (each link = 20 cm = 0.2 m). A 30 m metric chain has 150 links.

questions.question: 90° is set out using:
questions.explanation: An open cross-staff is used on survey lines to set out right angles (90°) for perpendicular offsets.

questions.question: ___________ angles can be set out using French cross staff.
questions.explanation: An octagonal French cross staff has sighting slits set at angles that allow setting out both 45° and 90° lines.

questions.question: Gunter's chain is ___________ in length.
questions.explanation: Gunter's chain (surveyor's chain) is 66 feet long and contains 100 links (1 link = 0.66 ft = 7.92 in).

questions.question: Survey related to large water bodies is called
questions.explanation: Hydrographic surveying encompasses surveys of water bodies (oceans, lakes, rivers, harbors) for navigation, bathymetry, and shorelines.

questions.question: Offsets are said to be large when offset length exceeds _________ m.
questions.explanation: In chain surveying, perpendicular offsets exceeding 15 meters in length are categorized as long offsets (short offsets are ≤ 15 m).

questions.question: A set of arrows provided with chain has _________ arrows.
questions.explanation: A standard set of survey arrows accompanying a metric chain consists of 10 arrows made of tempered 4 mm steel wire.

questions.question: Which of the following instrument is used for ranging ?
questions.explanation: A line ranger is an optical instrument consisting of two 90° reflecting prisms used for fixing intermediate ranging points without an assistant at the ends.

questions.question: The horizontal angle which a line makes with the meridian is called
questions.explanation: The horizontal angle measured between a survey line and a reference meridian (true, magnetic, or arbitrary) is defined as its bearing.

questions.question: The graduated ring being attached to the magnetic needle remains stationary in
questions.explanation: In a prismatic compass, the graduated aluminum ring is attached directly to the broad magnetic needle and remains stationary pointing magnetic North.

questions.question: In a prismatic compass 180° is marked at
questions.explanation: In a prismatic compass, 0° is engraved at the South end and 180° is at the North end so that the bearing can be read directly through the prism at the eye vane.

questions.question: The bearing of a line taken from the starting point of the line towards the direction in which survey progress is called
questions.explanation: The bearing of a survey line taken in the forward direction of progress of the survey from the starting station is called the Fore Bearing (FB).

questions.question: In the whole circle bearing systems, S 85°- 45' W will be expressed as
questions.explanation: S 85°-45' W lies in the 3rd quadrant (SW). WCB = 180° + 85°45' = 265°45'.

questions.question: At poles the magnetic dip is equal to
questions.explanation: Magnetic dip is the vertical inclination of the needle to the horizontal. It is 0° at the magnetic equator and 90° (vertical) at the magnetic poles.

questions.question: The whole circle bearing of a line observed by a prismatic compass is 110°, its bearing read on a surveyor's compass is
questions.explanation: A WCB of 110° lies in the 2nd quadrant (SE). Reduced Bearing (QB) = 180° - 110° = S 70° E.

questions.question: The horizontal angle which magnetic meridian makes with the true meridian is called
questions.explanation: Magnetic declination is the horizontal angle between the magnetic meridian and the true (geographical) meridian at a place.

questions.question: The line joining places of equal declination
questions.explanation: Isogonic lines are imaginary lines connecting points on the earth's surface that have the same magnetic declination. (Agonic lines have zero declination).

questions.question: The fore bearing of a line is S 45° 10' E find the back bearing
questions.explanation: To convert Fore Bearing to Back Bearing in Quadrantal system, retain numerical angle and reverse quadrant letters: S 45°10' E becomes N 45°10' W.

questions.question: The magnetic bearing of a line is 190° and the magnetic declination is 2° W. Find the true bearing of the line
questions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing ± Declination = 190° - 2° (West declination is subtracted) = 188°.

questions.question: The permissible error in prismatic compass survey is
questions.explanation: In prismatic compass surveying, the permissible error of closure is generally specified as 1 in 340 (or an angular limit of 20').

questions.question: Meridian joining earth's true north and south is called
questions.explanation: The true meridian is the imaginary great circle passing through the geographical north and south poles of the earth and the observer's position.

questions.question: Convert Q.B., S 45° 00' E into W.C.B.
questions.explanation: S 45° 00' E lies in the second quadrant (SE). WCB = 180° - 45°00' = 135° 00'.

questions.question: W.C.B. of a survey line is determined using
questions.explanation: A prismatic compass reads Whole Circle Bearings (0° to 360°) directly through its viewing prism.

questions.question: Theoretical sum of interior angles of a closed irregular hexagon is:
questions.explanation: The theoretical sum of interior angles of a closed polygon with n sides is (2n - 4) × 90°. For a hexagon (n = 6): (12 - 4) × 90° = 720°.

questions.question: Convert W.C.B. 320° 00' into Q.B.
questions.explanation: A WCB of 320° 00' lies in the 4th quadrant (NW). Reduced Bearing = 360° - 320°00' = N 40° 00' W.

questions.question: 0° is engraved at ___________ of the graduated ring of the prismatic compass.
questions.explanation: In a prismatic compass, 0° is graduated at the South end of the ring because reading is done through the prism at the diametrically opposite side.

questions.question: W.C.B. is always reckoned from
questions.explanation: Whole Circle Bearing (WCB) is always measured clockwise starting from the magnetic or true North direction.

questions.question: Magnetic bearing of a line determined was 140° but later it was found that Declination at the place is 2° W. Find the true bearing of the line.
questions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing ± Declination. Here Magnetic Bearing = 140°, Declination = 2° W. True Bearing = 140° - 2° = 138°.

questions.question: Change in declination at place happening in 24 hours is type of variation.
questions.explanation: Diurnal variation is the daily cyclic oscillation of the magnetic needle caused by the rotation of the earth and solar radiation over 24 hours.

questions.question: F.B. of RS is S 45° 15' E. F.B. of PR is S 30° 00' E. Included angle PRS measured in clockwise direction is:
questions.explanation: Included angle at station R: Computed from the back bearing of PR and forward bearing of RS; measured clockwise as 164° 45'.

questions.question: Magnetic equator is an example for
questions.explanation: The magnetic equator is an aclinic line where the magnetic dip is zero (the magnetic needle remains horizontal).

questions.question: F.B. of CD is 30°. FB of DE is 260°. Find ∠CDE measured in clockwise direction:
questions.explanation: Deflection angle / included angle between CD (FB = 30°) and DE (FB = 260°): Clockwise angle ∠CDE = 50°.

questions.question: Bearing measured in the direction of the progress of surveying is called
questions.explanation: The bearing of a survey line measured in the direction of the forward progress of the survey is the Fore Bearing (FB).

questions.question: F.B. of a line PQ is 140°. What is the F.B. of the line QP ?
questions.explanation: If Fore Bearing of PQ = 140°, the Fore Bearing of QP is its Back Bearing: BB = 140° + 180° = 320°.

questions.question: Vertical angle with which magnetic needle makes with the horizontal is called
questions.explanation: Magnetic dip is the vertical inclination that a freely suspended magnetic needle makes with the horizontal plane.

questions.question: Which method of plane table survey is also used for plotting the distant and inaccessible objects, broken boundaries, river etc?
questions.explanation: The intersection method in plane tabling is ideal for mapping distant, inaccessible points, river boundaries, and broken ground without measuring distances on ground.

questions.question: The process of putting the positions occupied by the board at various survey stations are kept parallel is known as
questions.explanation: Orientation is the process of keeping the plane table at each successive station parallel to the position it occupied at the first station.

questions.question: What is the name of method used in plane table survey similar to that of compass survey?
questions.explanation: Plane table traversing is similar to compass traversing, running a connected series of lines from station to station.

questions.question: Which type of survey cannot be done in dense wooded areas?
questions.explanation: Plane table surveying requires unobstructed sight lines and daylight; it cannot be effectively conducted in dense wooded forests or wet rainy climates.

questions.question: The three points problem may be solved by
questions.explanation: The three-point problem in plane tabling can be solved by mechanical (tracing paper), graphical (Bessel's / cutting arcs), and trial & error (Lehmann's) methods.

questions.question: Instrument used for sighting objects and drawing rays in plane tabling is
questions.explanation: An alidade (plain or telescopic) is the primary sighting and ray-drawing instrument used in plane table surveying.

questions.question: ___________ surveying can be performed without field book.
questions.explanation: In plane table surveying, observations and plotting are performed concurrently in the field on the drawing board, eliminating the need for a field notebook.

questions.question: Which of the following plane table method involves in finding an instrument station ?
questions.explanation: Resection is the plane table method where the position of an unknown occupied instrument station is located on the drawing board by sighting known visible stations.

questions.question: Bessel's solution to three point problem is related to
questions.explanation: Bessel's method of inscribed circles is an exact graphical solution to the three-point problem in plane tabling.

questions.question: Principle of plane table surveying is
questions.explanation: The fundamental principle of plane table surveying is orientation by parallelism, keeping the table board parallel to its orientation at preceding stations.

questions.question: What is the term that is normal to plumb line at all points?
questions.explanation: A level surface is a curved surface that is concentric with the mean spheroidal shape of the earth and perpendicular (normal) to the gravity plumb line at every point.

questions.question: What is the benchmarks established between the G.T.S. benchmarks by the state PWD is known as
questions.explanation: Permanent benchmarks are fixed, durable reference points established by government departments (PWD, Railways) between primary G.T.S. benchmarks.

questions.question: Which level is used for precise levelling work?
questions.explanation: A tilting level allows the telescope with its bubble tube to be tilted slightly in the vertical plane using a micrometer screw, making it suitable for precise levelling.

questions.question: In which staff consist of three parts and one slides into another?
questions.explanation: A Sopwith telescopic staff consists of three sliding telescopic lengths made of seasoned wood or aluminum, extending up to 4 or 5 meters.

questions.question: What is the smallest graduated division in levelling staff?
questions.explanation: The smallest graduation mark on a standard metric levelling staff is 5 mm (0.005 m).

questions.question: Which method of contour is suitable for small and undulating area?
questions.explanation: The square (grid) method is ideal for contouring small, undulating, and moderately flat building sites.

questions.question: Which method is not included in the interpolation of contours?
questions.explanation: Cross-sectioning is a field method used to collect elevation data, not an interpolation technique. Contour interpolation is performed by estimation, arithmetic calculation, or graphical methods.

questions.question: Combined correction for curvature and refraction is
questions.explanation: Combined correction for earth curvature and atmospheric refraction is C_comb = C_c - C_r = 0.0785 D² - 0.0112 D² = 0.0673 D² meters (where D is in km).

questions.question: What is the name of the staff 3m long and the band fitted is graduated in mm used for percise levelling?
questions.explanation: An invar levelling staff has an invar alloy ribbon fitted with millimeter graduations under spring tension, ensuring minimal thermal expansion for precise levelling.

questions.question: What R.F. is select for drawing town planning schemes, reservoirs etc?
questions.explanation: For reservoir surveys, town planning, and catchment mapping, small to intermediate representative fractions such as 1/5000 (or 1/2500) are standard.

questions.question: Contour lines of different elevations can unite to form one line in ______
questions.explanation: Contour lines of different elevations coalesce into a single line along a vertical cliff (and cross each other only in an overhanging cliff or cave).

questions.question: The method of indirect levelling in which the relative elevations of different points are obtained by measuring the vertical angles and horizontal distance is known as
questions.explanation: Trigonometrical levelling is an indirect method where the relative difference in elevation is computed from measured vertical angles and horizontal distances.

questions.question: What benchmark is established for short duration such as at the end of a day's work?
questions.explanation: A temporary benchmark (TBM) is established at the close of a day's work on a permanent object (culvert, rock) so that levelling can resume the next day.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to establishing grade contour?
questions.explanation: An Abney level is a hand-held clinometer/level used for measuring ground slope and setting out grade contours in road reconnaissance.

questions.question: Which is prismoidal formula for volume?
questions.explanation: The Prismoidal formula for volume between three equidistant parallel cross-sections of spacing L is V = (L / 6) × [A1 + 4A2 + A3].

questions.question: Boundary of a catchment area will be
questions.explanation: The natural boundary of a catchment/watershed basin separating drainage basins is the ridge line (watershed divide).

questions.question: Which of the following level's telescope can be rotated by surveyor in vertical plane in a smaller amount ?
questions.explanation: A tilting level possesses a micrometer tilting screw that tilts the telescope slightly in the vertical plane to level the line of sight precisely.

questions.question: Station where which B.S. and F.S. are taken is called
