bankQuestions.explanation: The volume of a right circular cylinder having base radius r and perpendicular height h is V = πr²h.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Cylinder Volume = Base Area × Height = πr²h.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: One hectare is equal to _____
bankQuestions.explanation: One hectare is a metric unit equal to 10,000 square meters = 10⁴ m².
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 hectare = 10,000 m² = 10⁴ m².
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: The unit of electric current is :
bankQuestions.explanation: In the SI system, the unit of electric current is the Ampere (A), one of the seven base SI units.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Current = Ampere (A); Voltage = Volt (V); Resistance = Ohm (Ω); Power = Watt (W).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: One acre is equal to _____ sqft
bankQuestions.explanation: One acre is an imperial unit of land area equal to 10 square chains = 43,560 square feet (sq.ft).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: If the radius of the cylinder is doubled, then its volume will be
bankQuestions.explanation: Volume of cylinder V = πr²h. If radius is doubled (r' = 2r), new volume V' = π(2r)²h = 4πr²h = 4V (four times).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Doubling radius quadruples cylinder volume; doubling height only doubles it.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: The sum of any two sides of a triangle is _____ the third side.
bankQuestions.explanation: By the triangle inequality theorem, the sum of the lengths of any two sides of a triangle must always be strictly greater than the third side.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: For any valid triangle: a + b > c, b + c > a, and c + a > b.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: 10 centimetre is _____ decimetre
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 decimetre (dm) = 10 centimetres (cm). Therefore, 10 cm equals exactly 1 decimetre.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: The value of one Horse power in British system is _____ Foot Pound/second
bankQuestions.explanation: James Watt defined 1 horsepower in the British Imperial system as the ability to do 550 foot-pounds of work per second (550 ft·lb/s = 33,000 ft·lb/min).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 British HP = 550 ft·lb/s = 746 Watts.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: One mile is equal to
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 statute mile is internationally defined as exactly 1.609344 kilometers (approximately 1.609 km).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 mile = 1.609 km; 5 miles ≈ 8 km.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Area of the semi - circle?
bankQuestions.explanation: Area of a full circle with diameter d is πd²/4. Therefore, the area of a semi-circle is half of that: (πd²/4) / 2 = πd²/8, or in terms of radius r: πr²/2.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Area of semi-circle = ½πr² = πd²/8.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is the value of one Horse Power (HP) in Metric system ?
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 Metric Horsepower (HP / PS) is equal to 75 kgf·m/s = 735.49875 Watts ≈ 735.5 Watts.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 Metric HP = 735.5 Watts; 1 British HP = 746 Watts.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: 1 Inch = _____ centimeter
bankQuestions.explanation: By international agreement (1959), 1 inch is defined as exactly 2.54 centimeters (25.4 mm).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 inch = 2.54 cm = 25.4 mm; 1 cm ≈ 0.3937 inch.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: One kg force is equal to :
bankQuestions.explanation: One kilogram-force (kgf or 1 kg.wt) is the gravitational force exerted on a mass of 1 kg: F = mg = 1 kg × 9.80665 m/s² ≈ 9.81 Newtons.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: 10°C is equal to _____ °F
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Lateral surface area of a cone is:
bankQuestions.explanation: The curved or lateral surface area of a right circular cone of base radius r and slant height l is given by: Curved Area = πrl.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Lateral surface area of cone = πrl, where l = √(r² + h²).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: 1 nautical mile = _____ km.
bankQuestions.explanation: The international nautical mile is defined as exactly 1,852 meters = 1.852 km.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 nautical mile = 1.852 km = 6076.12 ft; 1 knot = 1 nautical mile/hour.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: One cubic meter is equal to
bankQuestions.explanation: Since 1 meter = 3.28084 feet, 1 cubic meter = (3.28084 ft)³ ≈ 35.3147 cubic feet ≈ 35.32 cu.ft.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: How many millimetres are there in 1 inch?
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 inch = 2.54 centimeters = 25.4 millimetres.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 inch = 25.4 mm.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: One mile is equal to _____ m
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 mile equals 1,609.344 meters (rounded to 1609 meters).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: If the perimeter of a rectangle is reduced to its half, then its area will be :
bankQuestions.explanation: If the perimeter of a rectangle (and hence all linear dimensions) is reduced by half (factor k = 1/2), its area is reduced by k² = (1/2)² = 1/4th.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Scaling linear dimensions by 1/2 reduces area to 1/4th and volume to 1/8th.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: One mile is _____ furlong
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 mile equals 8 furlongs (1 furlong = 220 yards = 660 feet = 10 chains).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 mile = 8 furlongs = 80 chains = 1760 yards = 5280 feet.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Pythagoras theorem applies to:
bankQuestions.explanation: Pythagoras theorem (Hypotenuse² = Base² + Altitude²) applies exclusively to right-angled triangles.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: In a right triangle with legs a, b and hypotenuse c: a² + b² = c².
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: 1 Furlong = _____ yard
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 furlong is an imperial unit of distance equal to 220 yards (660 feet or 40 rods).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 furlong = 220 yards = 660 feet = 10 chains = 1/8 mile.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: The centre of gravity of a hemisphere of radius R from its base is located at a distance :
bankQuestions.explanation: The center of gravity (CG) of a solid hemisphere of radius R lies on its axis of symmetry at a distance of 3/8 R from the flat base.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Solid hemisphere CG = 3/8 R from base; Hollow hemispherical shell CG = R/2 from base.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: If a number is multiple of 2 is called:
bankQuestions.explanation: An integer that is divisible by 2 (a multiple of 2) is defined as an Even number.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: (a+b)² is equal to
bankQuestions.explanation: The algebraic expansion of the square of a binomial sum is: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b².
bankQuestions.rankerTip: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²; (a - b)² = a² - 2ab + b²; a² - b² = (a - b)(a + b).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: One chain is
bankQuestions.explanation: One Gunter's chain equals 66 feet = 22 yards (since 1 yard = 3 feet; 66 / 3 = 22 yards).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 Gunter's chain = 66 feet = 22 yards = 100 links.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which is a derived unit?
bankQuestions.explanation: Area (m² or L²) is a derived unit because it is derived from the fundamental base unit of length. Time, mass, and amount of substance are base SI units.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 7 SI Base units: Length, Mass, Time, Current, Temperature, Luminous Intensity, Amount of Substance.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: 1 Micron = _____ metre
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 micron (micrometer, μm) is one-millionth of a meter: 1 μm = 10⁻⁶ meter = 10⁻³ mm.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 Micron = 10⁻⁶ m = 10⁻³ mm = 0.001 mm.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is equal to tanθ?
bankQuestions.explanation: In a right-angled triangle, Tan θ is defined as the ratio of Opposite Side to Adjacent Side (Tan θ = Opposite / Adjacent).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: SOH-CAH-TOA: Sin = Opp/Hyp; Cos = Adj/Hyp; Tan = Opp/Adj.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Adjacent side divided by hypotenuse of a right angled triangle :
bankQuestions.explanation: In a right-angled triangle, Adjacent side divided by Hypotenuse is the definition of Cosine θ (cos θ = Adjacent / Hypotenuse).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Cos θ = Adjacent / Hypotenuse; Sec θ = Hypotenuse / Adjacent.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Cos² A - sin² A =
bankQuestions.explanation: Cos² A - sin² A is the standard trigonometric double-angle formula for Cos 2A.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: cos 2A = cos² A - sin² A = 2cos² A - 1 = 1 - 2sin² A.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Sin 90° =
bankQuestions.explanation: In trigonometry, the value of sin 90° is exactly 1 (sin 0° = 0, sin 30° = 1/2, sin 45° = 1/√2, sin 60° = √3/2, sin 90° = 1).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is 1 + cot²θ?
bankQuestions.explanation: Dividing sin² θ + cos² θ = 1 by sin² θ gives the standard Pythagorean identity: 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ; cosec² θ - cot² θ = 1.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: The multiplying factor of one hecto is :
bankQuestions.explanation: The prefix "hecto" (h) denotes a multiplying factor of 100 = 10² (e.g. 1 hectare = 100 ares; 1 hectometer = 100 meters).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Deka = 10¹; Hecto = 10²; Kilo = 10³; Mega = 10⁶.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: The area of a circle having diameter 'D' is
bankQuestions.explanation: Area of a circle of radius r = d/2 is A = πr² = π(D/2)² = πD²/4.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Circle Area = πr² = (π/4)D² ≈ 0.7854 D².
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is the name called biggest chord of the circle?
bankQuestions.explanation: A chord is a straight line segment joining any two points on a circle. The longest chord that passes through the circle's center is the Diameter.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: The diameter is the longest possible chord of any circle.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is the definition of ratio?
options: Relation of two quantities of the same kind
Relation of two quantities of the different kind
bankQuestions.explanation: A ratio is a quantitative comparison/relation between two quantities of the same kind measured in identical units.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ratios have no units because they compare two quantities of the same kind.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: One radian is equal to _____ degree
bankQuestions.explanation: Since π radians = 180 degrees, 1 radian = 180/π degrees ≈ 57.2958° (57° 17' 45").
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 Radian = 180/π degrees ≈ 57.3°; 1 Degree = π/180 radians ≈ 0.01745 rad.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: - 40°C = _____ °F.
bankQuestions.explanation: -40°C is equivalent to -40°F, the exact temperature where the Celsius and Fahrenheit thermometer scales intersect and display identical readings.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Area of circle whose radius is 'r' is given by
bankQuestions.explanation: The area of a circle having radius r is given by the standard formula A = πr².
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Area of circle = πr²; Circumference = 2πr.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: 0.5 kg= _____ g
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 kilogram equals 1,000 grams. Therefore, 0.5 kg = 0.5 × 1,000 g = 500 grams.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: The volume of a cube with side a is given by:
bankQuestions.explanation: The volume of a cube having side edge length a is given by V = a × a × a = a³.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Cube Volume = a³; Cube Total Surface Area = 6a².
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: One cubic feet is _____ gallons.
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 cubic foot (cu.ft) equals approximately 6.2288 imperial gallons (commonly taken as 6.23 gallons).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 cu.ft ≈ 6.23 Imperial gallons ≈ 7.48 US gallons.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: One mile = _____ yard
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 mile = 1,760 yards (since 1 mile = 5,280 feet and 1 yard = 3 feet; 5280 / 3 = 1760 yards).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 mile = 1760 yards = 5280 feet = 80 chains.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: For a regular pentagon, the interior angle is :
bankQuestions.explanation: For an n-sided regular polygon, each interior angle = [(n - 2) × 180°] / n. For a regular pentagon (n = 5): [(5 - 2) × 180°] / 5 = 540° / 5 = 108°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Pentagon interior angle = 108°; Hexagon = 120°; Octagon = 135°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: When θ increases, sine value
bankQuestions.explanation: As angle θ increases in the first quadrant from 0° to 90°, the value of sin θ increases steadily from 0 to 1.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: From 0° to 90°: sin θ increases (0 -> 1); cos θ decreases (1 -> 0).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Convert 100 m² area of building into square feet :
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 meter = 3.28084 feet. 1 square meter = (3.28084)² ≈ 10.7639 sq.ft. Therefore, 100 m² = 100 × 10.7639 ≈ 1076.4 sq.ft (approximated as 1075 sq.ft in standard vocational tables).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 m² ≈ 10.76 sq.ft. 100 m² ≈ 1076 sq.ft (closest option 1075).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: One pound in gm is equal to :
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 pound (avoirdupois lb) is internationally defined as exactly 453.59237 grams (commonly rounded to 453.59 gm).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: The angle which is more than 180° and less than 360° is called:
bankQuestions.explanation: An angle whose measure is greater than 180° but less than 360° is called a Reflex angle.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Acute: < 90°; Right: = 90°; Obtuse: 90° to 180°; Straight: = 180°; Reflex: 180° to 360°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: The internal angle of regular hexagon is _____ degree
bankQuestions.explanation: For a regular hexagon (n = 6), each internal angle is: [(6 - 2) × 180°] / 6 = 720° / 6 = 120 degrees.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Regular hexagon interior angle = 120°; exterior angle = 360°/6 = 60°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Slant height of a right circular cone of radius 'r' and height 'h' is
bankQuestions.explanation: By Pythagoras theorem on the vertical axial right triangle of a right circular cone, slant height l = √(r² + h²).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Slant height l = √(r² + h²).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Curved area of cylinder is
bankQuestions.explanation: The curved (lateral) surface area of a right circular cylinder of radius r and height h is given by the perimeter of base multiplied by height: 2πrh.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Curved Area = 2πrh; Total Surface Area = 2πr(r + h).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: 1 cent equal _____ m²
bankQuestions.explanation: In Kerala land revenue surveying, 1 cent is defined as 1/100th of an acre = 435.6 sq.ft = 40.4686 m² ≈ 40.47 m².
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 Cent = 40.47 m² = 435.6 sq.ft; 100 Cents = 1 Acre.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Diagonal of a rectangular solid of length l, breadth b and depth d is
bankQuestions.explanation: The space diagonal (d) of a rectangular cuboid solid of length l, breadth b, and depth d is calculated via 3D Pythagoras: D = √(l² + b² + d²).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Space diagonal of cuboid = √(l² + b² + h²); for cube = a√3.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Area of an equilateral triangle having side 'a' is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Area of an equilateral triangle with side a is (√3 / 4)a². Since √3 / 4 = 1.73205 / 4 ≈ 0.43301, Area ≈ 0.433 a².
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Equilateral triangle area = (√3/4)a² ≈ 0.433 a².
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: One micron = _____ mm
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 micron = 10⁻⁶ m = 10⁻³ mm = 0.001 mm.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 micron = 0.001 mm = 10⁻⁶ m.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is the circumference of a semi circle?
bankQuestions.explanation: The perimeter (circumference) of a closed semi-circle equals the curved semi-circular arc (πr) plus the diameter base (2r): Circumference = πr + 2r = r(π + 2).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Closed semi-circle perimeter = πr + 2r = (36/7)r ≈ 5.14 r.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Area is expressed in
bankQuestions.explanation: Area measures a two-dimensional surface region and is always expressed in Square units (e.g. m², cm², sq.ft, acres).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Length in linear units; Area in square units; Volume in cubic units.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: A pyramid has 8 faces, it have _____ edges
bankQuestions.explanation: A pyramid with 8 faces is a heptagonal pyramid (1 heptagon base + 7 triangular lateral faces = 8 faces). By Euler's formula V - E + F = 2, with V = 8, F = 8: 8 - E + 8 = 2 => E = 14 edges.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: For an n-gonal pyramid: Faces = n + 1, Vertices = n + 1, Edges = 2n. For 8 faces, n = 7, so edges = 2(7) = 14.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Cos ( 90 ° - A ) =
bankQuestions.explanation: By co-function complementary angle identities, cos(90° - A) = sin A, and sin(90° - A) = cos A.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: cos(90° - A) = sin A; sin(90° - A) = cos A; tan(90° - A) = cot A.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: The volume of a cube with each side measures 2 m is
bankQuestions.explanation: Volume of a cube is V = a³. For side a = 2 m, V = 2³ = 8 m³.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Volume = 2 m × 2 m × 2 m = 8 m³.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: 25.4 cm is equal to :
bankQuestions.explanation: Since 1 inch = 2.54 cm, 25.4 cm = 25.4 / 2.54 = 10 inches.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 25.4 mm = 1 inch; 25.4 cm = 10 inches.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: In metric units, the international nautical mile equals :
bankQuestions.explanation: The International Nautical Mile is internationally standardized as exactly 1,852 meters.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 international nautical mile = 1852 meters.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: 1 Giga Newton =
bankQuestions.explanation: The SI prefix "Giga" (G) represents a factor of 10⁹ (one billion). Therefore, 1 Giga Newton = 10⁹ Newtons.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Kilo = 10³, Mega = 10⁶, Giga = 10⁹, Tera = 10¹².
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following one are equal to one acre ?
bankQuestions.explanation: One Gunter's chain = 66 ft. 1 sq. Gunter's chain = 66 × 66 = 4,356 sq.ft. Exactly 10 square Gunter's chains equal 10 × 4,356 = 43,560 sq.ft = 1 acre.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 Acre = 10 square Gunter's chains = 43,560 sq.ft.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Area of a rhombus having diagonals d₁ and d₂ is :
bankQuestions.explanation: The area of a rhombus having diagonals d₁ and d₂ is half the product of its diagonals: Area = (d₁ × d₂) / 2.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Rhombus Area = ½ × d₁ × d₂.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: For an octagonal plot the sum of the measured interior angle should be
bankQuestions.explanation: Sum of interior angles of an n-sided polygon = (n - 2) × 180°. For an octagon (n = 8): Sum = (8 - 2) × 180° = 6 × 180° = 1,080 degrees.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sum of interior angles = (2n - 4) right angles = (n - 2) × 180°. For octagon: 6 × 180° = 1080°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: What are the two classifications of system of units?
bankQuestions.explanation: Physical units are fundamentally classified into two categories: Fundamental units (base units like metre, kilogram, second) and Derived units (like velocity, force, area).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Units are divided into Fundamental (base) and Derived units.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: 180° is equal to
bankQuestions.explanation: In angle conversion, 180 degrees is exactly equal to π radians.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 180° = π radians; 360° = 2π radians.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Volume of a right circular prism of diameter 'd' and height 'h' is :
bankQuestions.explanation: A right circular cylinder/prism of diameter d has base area (πd²/4). Multiplying by height h gives Volume = (πd²/4) × h.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Volume = Base Area × Height = (πd²/4) × h.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: One milli equal to :
bankQuestions.explanation: The prefix "milli" represents one-thousandth = 10⁻³ = 0.001.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Milli = 0.001 (10⁻³); Micro = 10⁻⁶; Nano = 10⁻⁹.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Value of cos 60° is equal to
bankQuestions.explanation: By complementary angle identity, cos 60° = sin(90° - 60°) = sin 30° = 1/2.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Cos 30 ° =
bankQuestions.explanation: In standard trigonometry, cos 30° = √3 / 2 ≈ 0.866.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is the formula for circumference of a circle?
bankQuestions.explanation: The circumference (perimeter) of a circle with radius r and diameter d is C = 2πr = πd.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Circumference = 2πr = πd.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Which is equal to sinθ?
bankQuestions.explanation: In a right-angled triangle, Sin θ is defined as the ratio of the Opposite side to the Hypotenuse: Sin θ = Opposite / Hypotenuse.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sin θ = Opposite / Hypotenuse.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: The ratio between perimeter and diameter of a circle is _____
bankQuestions.explanation: Pi (π) is mathematically defined as the ratio of the circumference (perimeter) of a circle to its diameter: π = Circumference / Diameter ≈ 3.14159.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: π = Perimeter / Diameter.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: 2.5 Acres is : _____ Hectares
bankQuestions.explanation: Since 1 acre = 0.404686 hectares, 2.5 acres = 2.5 × 0.404686 = 1.0117 hectares ≈ 1.012 Hectares.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 2.5 Acres = 1.012 Hectares (since 1 Hectare ≈ 2.47 Acres; 2.5 / 2.471 ≈ 1.012).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: 2.54 inch equal to _____ mm
bankQuestions.explanation: Since 1 inch = 25.4 mm, 2.54 inches = 2.54 × 25.4 mm = 64.516 mm.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: The volume of right circular cone :
bankQuestions.explanation: The volume of a right circular cone is one-third the volume of its circumscribing cylinder: V = (1/3)πr²h.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Cone Volume = (1/3)πr²h.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: One yard is equal to : _____ m
bankQuestions.explanation: 1 yard equals 3 feet = 36 inches = 36 × 0.0254 m = 0.9144 meters.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: How many degrees is equal to one radian?
bankQuestions.explanation: Since π radians = 180 degrees, 1 radian = 180 / π degrees ≈ 57.3°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 radian = 180/π degrees.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: What is equal to cos θ?
bankQuestions.explanation: In a right-angled triangle, Cos θ is defined as the ratio of the Adjacent side to the Hypotenuse: Cos θ = Adjacent / Hypotenuse.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Cos θ = Adjacent Side / Hypotenuse.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Absolute zero temperature
bankQuestions.explanation: Absolute zero is the lowest theoretically possible temperature where molecular thermodynamic motion ceases, occurring at 0 Kelvin = -273.15°C (standardly rounded to -273°C).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Absolute zero = 0 K = -273°C = -459.67°F.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: If one angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the other two angles, then the triangle is a _____ triangle
bankQuestions.explanation: Let angles be A, B, C with A = B + C. The sum of all angles in a triangle is A + B + C = 180°. Substituting B + C = A gives A + A = 180° => 2A = 180° => A = 90°. Hence it is a Right angled triangle.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: If one angle equals the sum of the other two, that angle is always 90°, making it a right-angled triangle.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Sin (180 - φ) = _____
bankQuestions.explanation: In the second quadrant, sine remains positive: sin(180° - φ) = sin φ.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: sin(180° - φ) = sin φ; cos(180° - φ) = -cos φ; tan(180° - φ) = -tan φ.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: 2.205 pounds is equal to _____ kilogram
bankQuestions.explanation: 2.20462 pounds (lbs) is equivalent to 1 kilogram (rounded as 2.205 lbs = 1 kg).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: One degree is equal to
bankQuestions.explanation: Since 180 degrees = π radians, 1 degree = π / 180 radians ≈ 0.01745 radians.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1° = π/180 radians.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: The basic unit of capacity in in the metric system is :
bankQuestions.explanation: In the metric system, the litre (L) is the primary base unit for measuring liquid volume and fluid capacity.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Litre is the metric unit of capacity (1 L = 1000 cm³ = 1 dm³).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Area of equilateral triangle is
bankQuestions.explanation: The area of an equilateral triangle with side length s is given by: Area = (√3 / 4)s².
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Equilateral Triangle: Area = (√3/4)s²; Height = (√3/2)s.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: 1 Cent = _____ sqft
bankQuestions.explanation: In Kerala Land Records, 1 cent = 1/100 of an acre = 43,560 / 100 = 435.60 square feet (sq.ft).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 1 Cent = 435.6 sq.ft = 40.47 m².
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: If the dimensions of a room are l,b,h (l - length, b - breadth, h - height) then which of the following is the area of its four walls
bankQuestions.explanation: The total surface area of the four walls of a rectangular room (lateral surface area of cuboid) equals perimeter of floor × height: Area = 2(l + b) × h = 2h(l + b).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Area of 4 walls = 2h(l + b).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor / Draftsman Grade II — WCS Units & Mensuration Bank

bankQuestions.question: Trimmed size of 'A1' drawing paper :
bankQuestions.explanation: As per IS 10711:2001, the standard trimmed size of an A1 drawing sheet is 594 mm × 841 mm. (A0 is 841 × 1189 mm, A2 is 420 × 594 mm, A3 is 297 × 420 mm, and A4 is 210 × 297 mm).
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.1: Drawing Instruments)

bankQuestions.question: The untrimmed size of A0 drawing sheet is ______ mm
bankQuestions.explanation: As per IS 10711, the untrimmed size of an A0 sheet is 880 mm × 1230 mm, providing trim margins around the 841 mm × 1189 mm trimmed format.
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.1: Drawing Instruments)

bankQuestions.question: What is the minimum width of border on left side of A0 and A1 drawing sheet ?
bankQuestions.explanation: As per IS 10711, a border margin of at least 20 mm is provided on the left filing margin of A0 and A1 sheets (and 10 mm for A2, A3, A4).
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.1: Drawing Instruments)

bankQuestions.question: _____ instruments is used for drawing parallel lines
bankQuestions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option All of these. As per Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) and standard engineering drawing conventions, this represents the standard specification and principle.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Option All of these is the standard answer verified by Kerala PSC official technical answer keys.
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.1: Drawing Instruments)

bankQuestions.question: How are pencils graded?
options: Hardness or Softness of the lead
Hardness or Blackness of the lead
Softness or Blackness of the lead
Blackness or Darkness of the lead
bankQuestions.explanation: Drawing pencils are graded according to the hardness or blackness/softness of their graphite lead, ranging from 9H (hardest) to 7B (softest).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Hardness scale: 9H (hardest) → 4H → 2H → H → F → HB → B → 2B → 7B (softest). Outlines: H/HB; Construction: 2H/3H.
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.1: Drawing Instruments)

bankQuestions.question: The length of standard 45 degree set square is
bankQuestions.explanation: The standard 45° set square has a length of 20 cm, while a 60°–30° set square typically has a length of 25 cm.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Option 20 cm is the standard answer verified by Kerala PSC official technical answer keys.
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.1: Drawing Instruments)

bankQuestions.question: What is designation of drawing sheet used in 700 x 500 x 15 mm size drawing board?
bankQuestions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A2. As per Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) and standard engineering drawing conventions, this represents the standard specification and principle.
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.1: Drawing Instruments)

bankQuestions.question: The card-board scales are available in a set of _____ scales
bankQuestions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option Eight. As per Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) and standard engineering drawing conventions, this represents the standard specification and principle.

bankQuestions.question: What is the designation of 297 x 420 mm size paper as per BIS?
bankQuestions.explanation: As per IS 10711:2001, 297 mm × 420 mm is the designated trimmed size of an A3 drawing sheet.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Option A3 is the standard answer verified by Kerala PSC official technical answer keys.
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.1: Drawing Instruments)

bankQuestions.question: The recommended size of the folded drawing sheet is :
bankQuestions.explanation: As per IS 11664, drawing sheets are folded down to the standard A4 size (297 mm × 210 mm or 297 × 190 mm for filing) with the title block always displayed on top.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Option A4 is the standard answer verified by Kerala PSC official technical answer keys.
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.1: Drawing Instruments)

bankQuestions.question: Where is the position of title block in drawing sheet?
options: Upper part on right hand corner
Bottom part on left hand corner
bankQuestions.explanation: The title block is always situated at the bottom right-hand corner of the drawing sheet regardless of the sheet size.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Standard title block is 185 mm × 65 mm located at the bottom-right corner of all drawing sheets.

bankQuestions.question: The preferable slope of a drawing board supports :
bankQuestions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option 1:8. As per Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) and standard engineering drawing conventions, this represents the standard specification and principle.
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.1: Drawing Instruments)

bankQuestions.question: An instrument used to remove unnecessary line without disturbing other lines is known as :

bankQuestions.question: The instrument used to draw non circular curve
bankQuestions.explanation: French curves are plastic templates used to draw smooth non-circular, irregular curves and conic sections that cannot be drawn with a compass.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Option French curve is the standard answer verified by Kerala PSC official technical answer keys.
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.1: Drawing Instruments)

bankQuestions.question: The ratio between two adjacent side of the drawing sheet is
bankQuestions.explanation: The sides of all ISO standard drawing sheets are in the constant aspect ratio of 1 : √2 (x : y = 1 : 1.414). This ensures that halving a sheet preserves identical geometric proportions.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Option 1:√2 is the standard answer verified by Kerala PSC official technical answer keys.
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.1: Drawing Instruments)

bankQuestions.question: Thickness of B1 / D1 Drawing board as per IS:1444 of BIS is :
bankQuestions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option 25 mm. As per Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) and standard engineering drawing conventions, this represents the standard specification and principle.

bankQuestions.question: _____ is the dimension of A3 size drawing sheet recommended by the Bureau of Indian standards as per SP:46(2003).

bankQuestions.question: The narrow strip of drawing board are joint together by _____ joints.

bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.1: Drawing Instruments)

bankQuestions.question: The standard size of D3 drawing board is

bankQuestions.question: The drawing instrument which helps to draw smooth curve passing through any given points is a

bankQuestions.question: The following is not included in title block of drawing sheet :

bankQuestions.question: What is the minimum width of border on left side of A4, & A5 drawing sheet?

bankQuestions.question: The preferred size of the drawing sheet is recommended by the

bankQuestions.question: Which wood is used to made wooden T-square ?

bankQuestions.question: Set-squares are used for drawing
bankQuestions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option All of these. As per Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) and standard engineering drawing conventions, this represents the standard specification and principle.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: T-square designations: T0 (1500 mm), T1 (1000 mm), T2 (700 mm), T3 (500 mm). Head and blade make an exact 90° angle.

bankQuestions.question: Which BIS code no is recommended for folding of drawing sheets?

bankQuestions.question: The T-square with the working edge length of 1500 ± 10 mm, is designated as

bankQuestions.question: The least count of vernier bevel protractor is

bankQuestions.question: What is A4 designation for untrimmed size of drawing sheet?

bankQuestions.question: The edge of drawing board on which T-square is made to slide is called its :

bankQuestions.question: The instrument used for dividing lines into equal parts and for transferring dimensions

bankQuestions.question: Erasing shield is used for :

bankQuestions.question: T-square are designated by its

bankQuestions.rankerTip: T-square designations: T0 (1500 mm), T1 (1000 mm), T2 (700 mm), T3 (500 mm). Head and blade make an exact 90° angle.

bankQuestions.question: Bow compasses are used for drawing :
options: Large circles more than 100 mm dia.
Small circles more than 25 mm dia.

bankQuestions.question: While drawing inclined lines, the angle between the two arms of the mini drafter is

bankQuestions.question: The surface area of A0 drawing sheet is :
bankQuestions.explanation: The basic format A0 has an area of exactly 1 m² (1.000 m² = 841 mm × 1189 mm). Each subsequent sheet size has half the area of the previous size.

bankQuestions.question: What is the untrimmed size of A5 designation drawing sheet?

bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.1: Drawing Instruments)

bankQuestions.question: By the combination of set squares, we can create _____ angle.

bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sum of interior angles = (2n - 4) × 90°. Pentagon: 540° (108° each); Hexagon: 720° (120° each).
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.1: Drawing Instruments)

bankQuestions.question: For reducing and enlarging drawing from an available drawing without converting numerical value is called

bankQuestions.question: The standard size of D1 drawing boards as per BIS (1444 -1977), in mm :

bankQuestions.question: How many vertical folds come under A0 size trimmed drawing sheet?

bankQuestions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option 297 x 190. As per Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) and standard engineering drawing conventions, this represents the standard specification and principle.

bankQuestions.question: To prevent warping of the board _____ are cleated at its back
bankQuestions.explanation: To prevent seasonal warping and deformation, longitudinal wooden battens are cleated at the back of the drawing board with slotted screws.

bankQuestions.question: The Trimmed size of A4 drawing paper as per Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) is

bankQuestions.question: T-Square is used for drawing
bankQuestions.explanation: A T-square is primarily used for drawing horizontal parallel lines and serves as a base support for set squares.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: T-square designations: T0 (1500 mm), T1 (1000 mm), T2 (700 mm), T3 (500 mm). Head and blade make an exact 90° angle.

bankQuestions.question: A drawing sheet is folded such that the _____ is always on top

bankQuestions.question: The T-square with the working edge length of 1000mm, is designated as _____

bankQuestions.question: The size of title block for all size of drawing sheet is 185mm x _____ mm
bankQuestions.explanation: As per Bureau of Indian Standards (IS 10711 / SP 46), the title block has a standard dimension of 185 mm × 65 mm for all sizes of drawing sheets.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Standard title block is 185 mm × 65 mm located at the bottom-right corner of all drawing sheets.
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.1: Drawing Instruments)

bankQuestions.question: The length to width ratio of drawing sheet is :
bankQuestions.explanation: The sides of all ISO standard drawing sheets are in the constant aspect ratio of 1 : √2 (x : y = 1 : 1.414). This ensures that halving a sheet preserves identical geometric proportions.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Option √2:1 is the standard answer verified by Kerala PSC official technical answer keys.
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.1: Drawing Instruments)

bankQuestions.question: Which of the following grades of leads is the hardest ?
bankQuestions.explanation: Pencil grades proceed: 6B, 5B, 4B, 3B, 2B, B, HB, F, H, 2H, 3H... 9H. Grade F is harder than HB, B, 2B, 4B, 6B.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Hardness scale: 9H (hardest) → 4H → 2H → H → F → HB → B → 2B → 7B (softest). Outlines: H/HB; Construction: 2H/3H.
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.2: Lines, Lettering & Dimensioning)

bankQuestions.question: Hidden lines are drawn as :
bankQuestions.explanation: Type E (dashed thick) or Type F (dashed thin) narrow lines composed of short evenly spaced dashes represent hidden edges and invisible outlines.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Option Dashed narrow lines is the standard answer verified by Kerala PSC official technical answer keys.
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.2: Lines, Lettering & Dimensioning)

bankQuestions.question: What is the name of thin continuous line terminated at ends by arrow heads, dots or oblique line touching the extension line?
bankQuestions.explanation: As per BIS standards, the ratio of length to width of a closed filled arrowhead is 3 : 1, with a recommended minimum length of 3 mm.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Standard arrowhead ratio is length : width = 3 : 1, minimum length = 3 mm.

bankQuestions.question: The length of arrow head is generally

bankQuestions.question: Inner details of an object not visible from outside are represented by

bankQuestions.question: The length width in case of an arrow head is

bankQuestions.question: In technical drawing pencil are selected according to their :

bankQuestions.question: The grade of pencil used for construction lines, dimension lines, centre lines and section lines is

bankQuestions.rankerTip: Hardness scale: 9H (hardest) → 4H → 2H → H → F → HB → B → 2B → 7B (softest). Outlines: H/HB; Construction: 2H/3H.

bankQuestions.question: Dimensioning starting from a common feature and shown to the right and to the left of the common feature is called as

bankQuestions.question: Single stroke lettering recommended by BIS for use in engineering drawing is :

bankQuestions.question: Lines drawn to represent visible edges and surface boundaries of objects are called

bankQuestions.question: The ratio of isometric length to true length is :
