bankQuestions.rankerTip: Isometric length = √(2/3) × True length ≈ 0.816 × True length (82%). Isometric view is ~22.5% larger than isometric projection.
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.6: Miscellaneous Questions)

bankQuestions.question: Obtuse angles is an angle :
bankQuestions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option Greater than 90°. As per Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) and standard engineering drawing conventions, this represents the standard specification and principle.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sum of interior angles = (2n - 4) × 90°. Pentagon: 540° (108° each); Hexagon: 720° (120° each).
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.6: Miscellaneous Questions)

bankQuestions.question: The curve generated by a point on the circumference of a circle rolling along a straight line is called a
bankQuestions.explanation: A cycloid is the curve generated by a point on the circumference of a circle that rolls along a straight line without slipping.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Option Cycloid is the standard answer verified by Kerala PSC official technical answer keys.
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.6: Miscellaneous Questions)

bankQuestions.question: What is the name of quadrilateral with four sides are equal and four angles are right angle?
bankQuestions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option Square. As per Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) and standard engineering drawing conventions, this represents the standard specification and principle.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sum of interior angles = (2n - 4) × 90°. Pentagon: 540° (108° each); Hexagon: 720° (120° each).
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.6: Miscellaneous Questions)

bankQuestions.question: How many sides and angles are in quadrilateral?
bankQuestions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option 4 sides and 4 angles. As per Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) and standard engineering drawing conventions, this represents the standard specification and principle.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sum of interior angles = (2n - 4) × 90°. Pentagon: 540° (108° each); Hexagon: 720° (120° each).
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.6: Miscellaneous Questions)

bankQuestions.question: What is the sum of Interior and Exterior angle for a polygon?
bankQuestions.explanation: For a regular pentagon (n = 5), each exterior deflection angle = 360° / 5 = 72° (Interior angle = 180° - 72° = 108°).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sum of interior angles = (2n - 4) × 90°. Pentagon: 540° (108° each); Hexagon: 720° (120° each).
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.6: Miscellaneous Questions)

bankQuestions.question: A polyhedron having a plane figure as a base and a number of triangular faces meeting at apex is called
bankQuestions.explanation: Correct Answer: Option A pyramid. As per Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) and standard engineering drawing conventions, this represents the standard specification and principle.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Platonic solids: Tetrahedron (4 triangles), Cube (6 squares), Octahedron (8 triangles), Dodecahedron (12 pentagons), Icosahedron (20 triangles).
bankQuestions.examName: Engineering Drawing Official Bank (Ch.6: Miscellaneous Questions)

bankQuestions.question: Which fundamental principle of surveying prevents the accumulation of errors across a network?
bankQuestions.explanation: The primary principle of surveying is 'working from whole to part'. By establishing major control framework first, local errors are contained within individual triangles and do not accumulate.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Working from whole to part localizes errors; working from part to whole magnifies errors.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Surveys conducted to establish the exact property lines and boundaries of land parcels are classified as:
bankQuestions.explanation: Cadastral surveys are specialized surveys undertaken to determine, re-establish, or demarcate legal boundary lines, fields, plots, and real estate ownership.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Cadastral = Property/land boundary surveys; Topographical = Natural/artificial relief features.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The curvature of the earth is taken into consideration when the area of the survey exceeds:
bankQuestions.explanation: In geodetic surveying, earth's spherical curvature is taken into account when the survey area exceeds 195.5 km² (or 250 km² in older conventions). Below this, plane surveying is assumed.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Spherical excess is only 1 second of arc for a spherical triangle of area 195.5 km².
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: A survey conducted to locate water bodies, harbors, shore lines, and soundings is known as:
bankQuestions.explanation: Hydrographic surveying deals with bodies of water such as rivers, lakes, reservoirs, harbors, and oceans, determining shorelines and bed contours through soundings.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Hydrographic = Water bodies & depth soundings; Astronomical = Celestial bodies.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The difference in length between a spherical arc of 18.5 km on the earth surface and its subtended chord is approximately:
bankQuestions.explanation: For an arc length of 18.5 km (about 11.5 miles) on the earth's surface, the difference between the arc and its subtended chord is only 1.52 cm (0.0152 m).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Arc of 18.5 km exceeds chord by just 1.52 cm; arc of 55.5 km exceeds chord by 4.5 cm.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Which scale enables the measurement of three consecutive dimensions or units such as metres, decimetres, and centimetres?
bankQuestions.explanation: A diagonal scale is used to represent three consecutive units (e.g., meters, decimeters, centimeters) or two units with fractional division up to two decimal places based on the principle of similar triangles.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plain scale = 2 dimensions; Diagonal scale = 3 dimensions; Scale of chords = angles without protractor.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: A vernier in which 'n' divisions of the vernier scale equal '(n - 1)' divisions of the primary main scale is called a:
bankQuestions.explanation: In a direct vernier, n divisions of the vernier scale are equal to (n - 1) divisions of the main scale, and divisions read in the same direction as the main scale.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Direct vernier: nv = (n-1)s (reads in same direction); Retrograde vernier: nv = (n+1)s (reads opposite).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: In a retrograde vernier, the direction of graduation on the vernier scale is:
options: Opposite to that of the main scale
bankQuestions.explanation: In a retrograde vernier, the graduations are numbered in the direction opposite to the graduations of the main scale because each vernier division is slightly larger than a main scale division.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Retrograde vernier division v = s(n+1)/n > s, so graduations run backward relative to main scale.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: If an old map drawn to a scale of 1 cm = 100 m has shrunk such that a line originally 10 cm now measures 9.5 cm, what is the shrinkage factor?
bankQuestions.explanation: Shrinkage Factor (SF) = Shrunk Length / Original Length = 9.5 cm / 10.0 cm = 0.95. Shrunk Scale = Original Scale × SF.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Shrinkage Factor = Shrunk length / Original length = Shrunk RF / Original RF.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: If the representative fraction (RF) of a survey map is 1:2500, what distance on the ground is represented by 4 cm on the map?
bankQuestions.explanation: Ground distance = 4 cm × 2500 = 10,000 cm = 100 meters.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Distance on ground = Map distance × Scale denominator.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: How many links are there in a standard 20-metre metric chain as per IS 1492?
bankQuestions.explanation: A standard 20 m metric chain consists of 100 links, with each link measuring exactly 20 cm (0.2 m) from centre to centre of connecting rings.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 20m chain = 100 links (0.2m each); 30m chain = 150 links (0.2m each).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: What is the length of one link in a standard 30-metre metric chain?
bankQuestions.explanation: Every link in both 20 m and 30 m metric chains has a uniform length of 20 cm (200 mm), measured between the centers of consecutive middle connecting rings.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: All metric chains (IS 1492) have 20 cm link length.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: Gunter's chain (Surveyor's chain) has a total length of:
bankQuestions.explanation: Gunter's chain is 66 feet long and contains 100 links, each link being 0.66 ft (7.92 inches). 10 square chains equal 1 acre, and 80 chains equal 1 mile.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Gunter's = 66 ft (100 links); Revenue = 33 ft (16 links); Engineer's = 100 ft (100 links).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: How many links are in a Revenue chain used commonly in cadastral land record measurements?
bankQuestions.explanation: A Revenue chain is 33 feet long and is divided into 16 links. Each link is 2 1/16 feet (2.0625 feet).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Revenue chain: 33 feet, 16 links. Used in Cadastral/Land revenue surveys.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The length of an Engineer's chain is:
bankQuestions.explanation: An Engineer's chain is 100 feet long and contains 100 links, with each link measuring exactly 1 foot.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Engineer's chain = 100 ft, 100 links (1 link = 1 ft).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: In a 20-metre metric chain, brass tallies with two teeth indicate a distance from the nearest handle of:
bankQuestions.explanation: In a 20 m metric chain: 5 m has 1 tooth, 10 m has a circular or 2-toothed tally, 15 m has 1 tooth from opposite end. For 20m, the central 10 m tally marks the midpoint.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tallies are marked at 5m intervals. For 20m chain: 5m (1 tooth), 10m (round/2-notch), 15m (1 tooth).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Brass rings are provided in metric chains at every interval of:
bankQuestions.explanation: Small circular brass rings are inserted at every 1-metre interval along the length of metric chains, except where tallies are placed at every 5 metres.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Brass rings at every 1 metre; Brass tallies at every 5 metres.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Which measuring tape is composed of an alloy of 36% nickel and 64% steel, offering an extremely low coefficient of thermal expansion?
bankQuestions.explanation: Invar tape is made of an alloy of 36% nickel and 64% steel. It possesses an extremely low coefficient of thermal expansion (around 0.00000012/°C), making it ideal for base line measurements in geodetic triangulations.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Invar = 36% Nickel + 64% Steel. Used for primary geodetic base line measurement.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: Metallic tapes are manufactured by weaving linen cloth reinforced with fine wires of:
bankQuestions.explanation: Metallic tapes are made of water-proofed linen fabric interwoven with fine brass, bronze, or copper wires to minimize stretching when pulled.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Metallic tape is linen reinforced with brass/copper wires (it is NOT made of pure metal).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The standard pull applied during the calibration of a 20 m metric chain as per Indian Standards is:
bankQuestions.explanation: As per IS 1492, the overall length of a 20 m or 30 m metric chain is verified under a standard pull of 8 kg (approx. 80 Newtons) at a standard temperature of 20°C.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Metric chain testing standard tension = 8 kg (80 N) at 20°C.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Permissible tolerance in the total length of a 20-metre metric chain when new is:
bankQuestions.explanation: As per IS standards, the permissible tolerance for a 20 m metric chain is ±5 mm when newly manufactured, and ±8 mm when in use in the field.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tolerance when new: 20m chain = ±5 mm; 30m chain = ±8 mm. In field: 20m = ±8 mm.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: Permissible tolerance for a 30-metre metric chain when newly supplied from manufacturer is:
bankQuestions.explanation: The permissible tolerance on the total length of a 30 m metric chain when tested under 80 N pull is ±8 mm.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 30m chain tolerance = ±8 mm.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: When a chain becomes too long due to wear at ring joints, the measured distance will be:
options: Shorter than true distance (Error negative, Correction positive)
Longer than true distance (Error positive, Correction negative)
bankQuestions.explanation: If a chain is too long, it records fewer chain lengths over a line; hence, measured distance is shorter than actual. The error is negative, and the required correction is positive (+).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Too long chain: Measured < True -> Error (-), Correction (+).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: If a chain becomes too short due to bent links or mud clogging, the measured length of a line is:
bankQuestions.explanation: When a chain is too short, more chain lengths are required to span the distance; thus, the recorded distance is greater than the true distance. Error is positive (+), Correction is negative (-).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Too short chain: Measured > True -> Error (+), Correction (-).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: The true length of a measured line is calculated by the formula:
bankQuestions.explanation: True Length = (Actual length of chain L' / Designated length of chain L) × Measured Length.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: True Length = (L' / L) × Measured Length. True Area = (L' / L)² × Measured Area.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: A line was measured with a 20 m chain and found to be 400 m. Later, the chain was discovered to be 10 cm too long. What is the true length of the line?
bankQuestions.explanation: Actual chain length L' = 20.10 m, nominal L = 20 m. True length = (20.10 / 20) × 400 = 1.005 × 400 = 402.0 m.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: If a field area of 10,000 m² is measured with a chain that is 0.5% too short, the true area of the field is:
bankQuestions.rankerTip: True Area ≈ (1 - 2 × error ratio) × Area = (1 - 0.01) × 10,000 = 9,900 m².
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: Which adjustment should be made if a metric chain is found to be too long?
options: Closing up the joints of connecting rings that have opened out
Replacing small rings with larger oval rings
bankQuestions.explanation: When a chain is too long, the remedy is to close opened connecting rings, flatten elongated rings, or remove one or more small circular rings.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Too long: close joints, remove rings. Too short: straighten links, insert rings.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Arrows used in chain surveying are made of tempered steel wire of diameter:
bankQuestions.explanation: Arrows (chain pins) are made of good quality tempered steel wire of 4 mm diameter, with an overall length of 400 mm and a curved loop of 50 mm internal diameter.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Arrow wire diameter = 4 mm; total length = 400 mm; 10 arrows per chain set.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: How many arrows are officially supplied with a chain in standard survey practice?
bankQuestions.explanation: A standard set accompanying a surveyor's chain consists of 10 arrows.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 10 arrows are carried by the follower.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: Ranging rods are typically painted with alternate bands of red and white, each band having a length of:
bankQuestions.explanation: Ranging rods of 2 m or 3 m length are painted alternately in red and white (or black and white) bands of 20 cm (200 mm) each, which can also be used for rough estimation of short distances.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ranging rod bands = 20 cm (0.2 m). Ranging rod length = 2 m or 3 m.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Wooden pegs used in chain surveying to mark stations on the ground typically have a cross-section of:
bankQuestions.explanation: Wooden pegs are made of seasoned hard wood, 15 cm long with a tapered end, having a 2.5 cm to 3 cm square cross-section, driven into the ground leaving about 4 cm projecting.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Pegs: 15 cm length, 2.5 to 3 cm square cross-section.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: An offset rod differs from a ranging rod primarily because it has:
options: A hook or notch at the top for pulling chain through bushes
bankQuestions.explanation: An offset rod is a round wooden rod 3 m long with an iron shoe at bottom and a hook/groove at top used to pull chain through dense hedges or bushes and line short perpendiculars.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Offset rod has a top hook/groove to pull chain through brush.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: The process of establishing intermediate points on a straight line between two distant survey stations is termed:
bankQuestions.explanation: Ranging is the operation of aligning and fixing intermediate ranging rods on a straight survey line between two terminal stations prior to chaining.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Ranging = Aligning intermediate points on a straight line.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: When two survey stations are not mutually intervisible due to a high ridge or rising hill, the method employed to align the line is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Reciprocal or indirect ranging is adopted when the ends of a survey line are not intervisible due to an intervening hill or ridge, using two surveyors who alternately guide each other into line.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Reciprocal ranging = Indirect ranging used when stations are not intervisible due to a hill.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: An optical square is based on the optical principle of:
bankQuestions.explanation: The optical square functions on the principle of double reflection. The angle between the two reflecting surfaces is 45°, which produces an exact deflection of 90° for the reflected ray.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Optical square angle between mirrors = 45°; Deflection angle = 2 × 45° = 90° (Double reflection).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: The angle between the index glass and the horizon glass in an optical square is strictly fixed at:
bankQuestions.explanation: The two mirrors in an optical square are set at an exact angle of 45° to each other so that a ray reflected successively from both mirrors is turned through twice this angle, i.e., 2 × 45° = 90°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Mirrors inclined at 45° deflect rays by 90°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: In an optical square, which mirror is half silvered and half left completely clear/transparent?
bankQuestions.explanation: The horizon glass is silvered on its bottom half and transparent on its top half to allow simultaneous viewing of the direct ranging rod and the reflected offset rod.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Horizon glass = Half silvered, half clear. Index glass = Fully silvered.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Which cross-staff enables setting out lines at angles of 45°, 90°, and 135°?
bankQuestions.explanation: The French cross-staff consists of an octagonal brass hollow tube with sighting slits on all eight faces, enabling lines of sight at angles of 45°, 90°, and 135°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: French cross-staff = 45°, 90°, 135°; Open cross-staff = 90° only.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: An open cross-staff is used for:
bankQuestions.explanation: An open cross-staff has two pairs of vertical sighting slits oriented at exactly 90° to each other, used exclusively for setting out perpendicular offsets.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Open cross-staff sets out right angles (90°).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The sag correction for a tape suspended in catenary between two supports is:
options: Positive or negative depending on pull
Zero if tension is under 80 N
bankQuestions.explanation: A tape supported only at ends sags in a catenary, making the straight-line chord shorter than the tape curve. Hence, sag correction Cs = - (W² L) / (24 P²) is always negative.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sag correction is ALWAYS negative. Formula: Cs = - W² L / (24 P²).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The slope correction for a line of length 'L' with a height difference 'h' between its ends is approximately:
bankQuestions.explanation: The slope correction Ch = L - √(L² - h²) ≈ h² / (2L). It is always subtractive (negative) from the measured sloping distance.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Slope correction Ch = h² / (2L) (subtractive).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: The pull correction for a tape subjected to a tension 'P' different from standard calibration tension 'P₀' is given by:
bankQuestions.explanation: Pull (tension) correction Cp = (P - P₀) L / (A E), where A is cross-sectional area and E is Young's modulus of elasticity.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Pull correction: Cp = (P - P₀) L / (A E). Positive if P > P₀, negative if P < P₀.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Hypotenusal allowance per chain length of 100 links on a ground sloping at angle 'θ' is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Hypotenusal allowance is the additional distance along the slope required to cover exactly one horizontal chain length. Allowance = 100 (sec θ - 1) links.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Hypotenusal allowance = 100 (sec θ - 1) links.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Compensating errors in chaining are proportional to:
bankQuestions.explanation: Compensating (accidental/random) errors follow the laws of probability and are proportional to the square root of the length of the line (√L). Cumulative errors are directly proportional to L.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Compensating errors ∝ √L; Cumulative errors ∝ L.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: The longest survey line passing through the center of the survey area upon which the primary triangulation framework is built is termed:
bankQuestions.explanation: The base line is the most important and longest line laid across the center of the area, measured with highest accuracy, forming the backbone of the framework.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Base line = Longest main line forming backbone of survey.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: A survey line run to verify the accuracy of the framework and detect any errors in plotting is called a:
bankQuestions.explanation: A check line (or proof line) is a line measured to check the accuracy of the field work and framework. If its measured length matches its plotted length, the survey is accurate.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Check line / Proof line checks the accuracy of triangle plotting.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: A survey line run to fix internal details and features located away from the main chain lines is called a:
bankQuestions.explanation: A tie line connects tie stations on main survey lines and enables taking short offsets to interior objects, avoiding excessively long and inaccurate offsets.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Tie line fixes interior details and also acts as a check line.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: In a survey field book, bookings are entered starting from:
options: Bottom of the page and working upwards
Top of the page working downwards
bankQuestions.explanation: Entries in a field book start from the bottom of the page and proceed upwards, mimicking the surveyor walking forward along the chain line.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Field book entries always start from bottom and proceed upwards.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: In a double-line field book, the space between the two central lines is reserved for:
bankQuestions.explanation: In a double line field book, two red or blue lines spaced 15 mm to 20 mm apart represent the chain line, and chainage readings are written strictly inside this column.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Double line book: Chainages written inside the central column.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: A pond or river across a survey line represents an obstacle to:
bankQuestions.explanation: A pond or river can be seen across clearly, so vision (ranging) is free, but chaining cannot be performed directly on water; hence, it is an obstacle to chaining only.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: River/pond = Chaining obstructed, ranging free. Hill = Ranging obstructed, chaining free.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: A high building situated across a survey line represents an obstacle to:
bankQuestions.explanation: A building prevents both line of sight and linear chain measurement across it; therefore, it is an obstacle to both chaining and ranging.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Building = Both chaining and ranging obstructed.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Simpson's 1/3rd rule for computing boundary areas assumes that the boundary between ordinates is a:
bankQuestions.explanation: Simpson's rule assumes that the irregular boundary curve consists of parabolic arcs between successive groups of three ordinates.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Simpson's rule assumes parabolic arcs; Trapezoidal rule assumes straight lines.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Simpson's rule is applicable only when the total number of ordinates is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Simpson's 1/3rd rule requires dividing the area into pairs of strips; hence, there must be an even number of intervals and an odd number of ordinates.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Simpson's rule requires an ODD number of ordinates (EVEN number of intervals).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: What is the Representative Fraction (R.F.) of a survey map if a length of 5 cm on the plan represents 250 metres on the ground?
bankQuestions.explanation: RF = Map Distance / Ground Distance = 5 cm / (250 × 100 cm) = 5 / 25000 = 1:5000.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Representative Fraction (RF) must always have both numerator and denominator in the same units, with numerator as 1.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: What is the Representative Fraction (R.F.) of a survey map if a length of 2 cm on the plan represents 50 metres on the ground?
bankQuestions.explanation: RF = Map Distance / Ground Distance = 2 cm / (50 × 100 cm) = 2 / 5000 = 1:2500.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Representative Fraction (RF) must always have both numerator and denominator in the same units, with numerator as 1.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: A distance of 250 m was measured using a 30 m metric chain. If the chain was found to be 7 cm too long after testing, what is the corrected true length?
bankQuestions.explanation: True Length = (Actual Chain Length / Designated Length) × Measured Length = (30.07 / 30) × 250 = 250.58 m.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: When chain is too long, correction is positive: True = Measured + (e/L) × Measured.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: What is the Representative Fraction (R.F.) of a survey map if a length of 4 cm on the plan represents 1000 metres on the ground?
bankQuestions.explanation: RF = Map Distance / Ground Distance = 4 cm / (1000 × 100 cm) = 4 / 100000 = 1:25000.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Representative Fraction (RF) must always have both numerator and denominator in the same units, with numerator as 1.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: A distance of 300 m was measured using a 20 m metric chain. If the chain was found to be 9 cm too long after testing, what is the corrected true length?
bankQuestions.explanation: True Length = (Actual Chain Length / Designated Length) × Measured Length = (20.09 / 20) × 300 = 301.35 m.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: When chain is too long, correction is positive: True = Measured + (e/L) × Measured.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: What is the Representative Fraction (R.F.) of a survey map if a length of 10 cm on the plan represents 100 metres on the ground?
bankQuestions.explanation: RF = Map Distance / Ground Distance = 10 cm / (100 × 100 cm) = 10 / 10000 = 1:1000.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Representative Fraction (RF) must always have both numerator and denominator in the same units, with numerator as 1.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: A distance of 350 m was measured using a 30 m metric chain. If the chain was found to be 11 cm too long after testing, what is the corrected true length?
bankQuestions.explanation: True Length = (Actual Chain Length / Designated Length) × Measured Length = (30.11 / 30) × 350 = 351.28 m.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: When chain is too long, correction is positive: True = Measured + (e/L) × Measured.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: What is the Representative Fraction (R.F.) of a survey map if a length of 1 cm on the plan represents 200 metres on the ground?
bankQuestions.explanation: RF = Map Distance / Ground Distance = 1 cm / (200 × 100 cm) = 1 / 20000 = 1:20000.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Representative Fraction (RF) must always have both numerator and denominator in the same units, with numerator as 1.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III / PWD Draftsman

bankQuestions.question: A distance of 400 m was measured using a 20 m metric chain. If the chain was found to be 13 cm too long after testing, what is the corrected true length?
bankQuestions.explanation: True Length = (Actual Chain Length / Designated Length) × Measured Length = (20.13 / 20) × 400 = 402.60 m.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: When chain is too long, correction is positive: True = Measured + (e/L) × Measured.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The horizontal angle between the true meridian and the magnetic meridian at a place is termed:
bankQuestions.explanation: Magnetic declination is the angle on the horizontal plane between True North (geographic meridian) and Magnetic North (magnetic meridian).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Declination = Horizontal angle between True & Magnetic meridian; Dip = Vertical angle of needle.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: A line passing through points of zero magnetic declination on the earth's surface is called:
bankQuestions.explanation: An Agonic line is a line connecting points having zero magnetic declination. Lines connecting points of equal declination are Isogonic lines.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Agonic = Zero declination; Isogonic = Equal declination; Aclinic = Zero dip; Isoclinic = Equal dip.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The angle of dip of a freely suspended magnetic needle at the magnetic equator is:
bankQuestions.explanation: At the magnetic equator, the magnetic lines of force run parallel to the earth's surface, so the needle remains horizontal and the angle of dip is 0°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Dip is 0° at magnetic equator and 90° at magnetic poles.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning

bankQuestions.question: The angle of dip of a magnetic needle at the magnetic poles of the earth is:
bankQuestions.explanation: At the magnetic poles, magnetic lines of force enter vertically into the earth; therefore, a freely balanced needle points vertically downwards with dip = 90°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Dip at poles = 90° (vertical needle).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The line joining points on the earth surface having equal magnetic dip is known as:
bankQuestions.explanation: Isoclinic lines are imaginary contour lines joining places on the earth's surface that have the same angle of magnetic dip.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Isoclinic = Equal dip. Aclinic = Zero dip (magnetic equator).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: In a Prismatic Compass, the graduations on the aluminum ring are numbered:
options: Clockwise with 0° at South, 90° at West, 180° at North, 270° at East
Clockwise with 0° at North, 90° at East, 180° at South, 270° at West
Quadrantal with 0° at North and South
bankQuestions.explanation: In a prismatic compass, the ring is graduated clockwise starting with 0° at the South end, 90° at West, 180° at North, and 270° at East, with inverted figures read through a prism.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Prismatic compass: 0° is at SOUTH, West is 90°, North is 180°, East is 270°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning

bankQuestions.question: The least count of a standard Prismatic Compass is:
bankQuestions.explanation: A prismatic compass is graduated to 30 minutes (half a degree), which is its least count.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Prismatic Compass least count = 30'; Surveyor's Compass least count = 15'.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The least count of a standard Surveyor's Compass is:
bankQuestions.explanation: A Surveyor's compass is graduated in quadrants from 0° to 90° with a least count of 15 minutes.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Surveyor's Compass least count = 15'.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: In a Surveyor's Compass, the letters East and West on the dial are:
options: Transposed (East is to the left of North, West to the right)
bankQuestions.explanation: In a Surveyor's Compass, the graduated ring is fixed to the box and rotates with the sights. To read bearings directly from the needle tip, East and West are transposed (interchanged).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: In Surveyor's Compass, E and W are transposed on the dial.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning

bankQuestions.question: Which compass uses an edge-bar needle and can only be used with a tripod?
bankQuestions.explanation: A Surveyor's compass uses an edge-bar needle floating above the dial and must be supported on a tripod, whereas a prismatic compass has a broad needle and can be held in hand.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Surveyor's compass = Edge-bar needle, requires tripod. Prismatic = Broad needle.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Convert the Whole Circle Bearing (WCB) of 135° 30' into Quadrantal Bearing (QB):
bankQuestions.explanation: 135° 30' lies in the SE quadrant (2nd quadrant). QB = S (180° - 135° 30') E = S 44° 30' E.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Convert the Whole Circle Bearing (WCB) of 225° 45' into Quadrantal Bearing (QB):
bankQuestions.explanation: 225° 45' lies in the SW quadrant (3rd quadrant). QB = S (225° 45' - 180°) W = S 45° 45' W.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning

bankQuestions.question: Convert the Whole Circle Bearing (WCB) of 315° 15' into Quadrantal Bearing (QB):
bankQuestions.explanation: 315° 15' lies in the NW quadrant (4th quadrant). QB = N (360° - 315° 15') W = N 44° 45' W.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Convert the Quadrantal Bearing S 30° 15' W into Whole Circle Bearing (WCB):
bankQuestions.explanation: S 30° 15' W is in the 3rd quadrant. WCB = 180° + 30° 15' = 210° 15'.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: If the Fore Bearing (FB) of a line AB is 45° 30', its Back Bearing (BB) is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Back Bearing = Fore Bearing ± 180°. Since FB < 180°, BB = 45° 30' + 180° = 225° 30'.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning

bankQuestions.question: If the Fore Bearing of a line is S 25° 30' W in quadrantal system, its Back Bearing is:
bankQuestions.explanation: In the quadrantal system, the numerical value remains identical; simply substitute N for S and E for W. Thus, BB = N 25° 30' E.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: In QB, reverse cardinal letters: S -> N, W -> E.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: If the magnetic bearing of a line is 48° 24' and the magnetic declination is 5° 36' East, the true bearing of the line is:
bankQuestions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing + Declination East = 48° 24' + 5° 36' = 54° 00'.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing + East Declination (Add East, Subtract West).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: If the magnetic bearing of a line is 120° 30' and the magnetic declination is 3° 15' West, the true bearing is:
bankQuestions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing - Declination West = 120° 30' - 3° 15' = 117° 15'.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Subtract West declination: 120°30' - 3°15' = 117°15'.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning

bankQuestions.question: At magnetic noon, the true bearing of the sun in the northern hemisphere is:
bankQuestions.explanation: At solar noon, the sun is directly on the geographical meridian due South (in Northern hemisphere); hence, its true bearing is 180°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: True bearing of sun at noon in northern hemisphere = 180° (due South).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Local attraction at a survey station is detected when the difference between the Fore Bearing and Back Bearing of a line is:
bankQuestions.explanation: In the absence of local attraction and observational errors, |FB - BB| must equal exactly 180°. Any deviation indicates local magnetic attraction.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: |FB - BB| ≠ 180° indicates local attraction.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The sum of all interior angles of a closed polygon traverse with 'n' sides is given by:
bankQuestions.explanation: The theoretical sum of the interior angles of an n-sided closed polygon is (2n - 4) × 90° or (n - 2) × 180°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sum of interior angles = (2n - 4) × 90°; Sum of exterior angles = (2n + 4) × 90°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning

bankQuestions.question: The sum of all exterior angles of a closed polygon traverse having 'n' sides is:
bankQuestions.explanation: The sum of exterior angles of an n-sided closed polygon is (2n + 4) × 90°.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Exterior angles sum = (2n + 4) × 90°.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Bowditch's graphical method for adjusting closing error in a compass traverse is based on the assumption that:
options: Errors in linear measurements are proportional to √L and equal in precision to angular measurements
Linear measurements are much more precise than angular measurements
Angular measurements are completely free from error
Closing error is purely due to magnetic dip
bankQuestions.explanation: Bowditch's rule (Compass rule) assumes that errors in linear measurements are proportional to √l, errors in angular measurements are proportional to 1/√l, and linear and angular measurements have equal precision.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bowditch's rule balances linear and angular errors equally; graphical method adjusts each station proportionally.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Diurnal variation of magnetic declination is greater:
options: During summer than in winter, and during day than at night
At the equator than near magnetic poles
During the night than during the day
bankQuestions.explanation: Diurnal (daily) variation is caused by solar radiation affecting the ionosphere. It is greater during daytime than at night, greater in summer than winter, and increases towards the poles.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Diurnal variation: Summer > Winter; Day > Night; Poles > Equator.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning

bankQuestions.question: Secular variation of magnetic declination refers to:
options: A periodic cyclical swing taking hundreds of years like a pendulum
Sudden variations caused by magnetic storms
bankQuestions.explanation: Secular variation is a long-period cyclic oscillation of the magnetic meridian resembling the swing of a pendulum, with cycles typically spanning 250 to 300 years.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Secular variation = Long period swing (250-300 years).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: If the Whole Circle Bearing of a line is 142° 45', its equivalent Quadrantal Bearing (Reduced Bearing) is:
bankQuestions.explanation: For WCB = 142° 45', the line lies in quadrant with corresponding reduced angle giving S 38° 15' E.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Q1: N θ E; Q2: S (180-θ) E; Q3: S (θ-180) W; Q4: N (360-θ) W.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning

bankQuestions.question: If the Whole Circle Bearing of a line is 205° 00', its equivalent Quadrantal Bearing (Reduced Bearing) is:
bankQuestions.explanation: For WCB = 205° 00', the line lies in quadrant with corresponding reduced angle giving S 25° 00' W.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Q1: N θ E; Q2: S (180-θ) E; Q3: S (θ-180) W; Q4: N (360-θ) W.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: If the Whole Circle Bearing of a line is 235° 15', its equivalent Quadrantal Bearing (Reduced Bearing) is:
bankQuestions.explanation: For WCB = 235° 15', the line lies in quadrant with corresponding reduced angle giving S 55° 15' W.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Q1: N θ E; Q2: S (180-θ) E; Q3: S (θ-180) W; Q4: N (360-θ) W.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: If the Whole Circle Bearing of a line is 290° 30', its equivalent Quadrantal Bearing (Reduced Bearing) is:
bankQuestions.explanation: For WCB = 290° 30', the line lies in quadrant with corresponding reduced angle giving N 70° 30' W.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Q1: N θ E; Q2: S (180-θ) E; Q3: S (θ-180) W; Q4: N (360-θ) W.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning

bankQuestions.question: The magnetic bearing of a line is measured as 41° 30'. If the magnetic declination at the observation station is 3° 00' West, what is the true bearing of the line?
bankQuestions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing - Declination West = 41° 30' - 3° 00' = 38° 30'.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Always remember the thumb rule: Add East declination, Subtract West declination.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: If the Whole Circle Bearing of a line is 15° 00', its equivalent Quadrantal Bearing (Reduced Bearing) is:
bankQuestions.explanation: For WCB = 15° 00', the line lies in quadrant with corresponding reduced angle giving N 15° 00' E.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Q1: N θ E; Q2: S (180-θ) E; Q3: S (θ-180) W; Q4: N (360-θ) W.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: If the Whole Circle Bearing of a line is 160° 15', its equivalent Quadrantal Bearing (Reduced Bearing) is:
bankQuestions.explanation: For WCB = 160° 15', the line lies in quadrant with corresponding reduced angle giving S 20° 45' E.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Q1: N θ E; Q2: S (180-θ) E; Q3: S (θ-180) W; Q4: N (360-θ) W.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: If the Whole Circle Bearing of a line is 245° 30', its equivalent Quadrantal Bearing (Reduced Bearing) is:
bankQuestions.explanation: For WCB = 245° 30', the line lies in quadrant with corresponding reduced angle giving S 65° 30' W.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Q1: N θ E; Q2: S (180-θ) E; Q3: S (θ-180) W; Q4: N (360-θ) W.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning

bankQuestions.question: If the Whole Circle Bearing of a line is 340° 45', its equivalent Quadrantal Bearing (Reduced Bearing) is:
bankQuestions.explanation: For WCB = 340° 45', the line lies in quadrant with corresponding reduced angle giving N 20° 15' W.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Q1: N θ E; Q2: S (180-θ) E; Q3: S (θ-180) W; Q4: N (360-θ) W.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The magnetic bearing of a line is measured as 52° 30'. If the magnetic declination at the observation station is 4° 00' East, what is the true bearing of the line?
bankQuestions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing + Declination East = 52° 30' + 4° 00' = 56° 30'.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Always remember the thumb rule: Add East declination, Subtract West declination.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: If the Whole Circle Bearing of a line is 72° 15', its equivalent Quadrantal Bearing (Reduced Bearing) is:
bankQuestions.explanation: For WCB = 72° 15', the line lies in quadrant with corresponding reduced angle giving N 72° 15' E.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Q1: N θ E; Q2: S (180-θ) E; Q3: S (θ-180) W; Q4: N (360-θ) W.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: If the Whole Circle Bearing of a line is 118° 30', its equivalent Quadrantal Bearing (Reduced Bearing) is:
bankQuestions.explanation: For WCB = 118° 30', the line lies in quadrant with corresponding reduced angle giving S 62° 30' E.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Q1: N θ E; Q2: S (180-θ) E; Q3: S (θ-180) W; Q4: N (360-θ) W.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning

bankQuestions.question: The magnetic bearing of a line is measured as 63° 30'. If the magnetic declination at the observation station is 5° 00' West, what is the true bearing of the line?
bankQuestions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing - Declination West = 63° 30' - 5° 00' = 58° 30'.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Always remember the thumb rule: Add East declination, Subtract West declination.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning

bankQuestions.question: If the Whole Circle Bearing of a line is 325° 45', its equivalent Quadrantal Bearing (Reduced Bearing) is:
bankQuestions.explanation: For WCB = 325° 45', the line lies in quadrant with corresponding reduced angle giving N 35° 15' W.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Q1: N θ E; Q2: S (180-θ) E; Q3: S (θ-180) W; Q4: N (360-θ) W.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The magnetic bearing of a line is measured as 74° 30'. If the magnetic declination at the observation station is 6° 00' East, what is the true bearing of the line?
bankQuestions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing + Declination East = 74° 30' + 6° 00' = 80° 30'.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Always remember the thumb rule: Add East declination, Subtract West declination.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: If the Whole Circle Bearing of a line is 35° 00', its equivalent Quadrantal Bearing (Reduced Bearing) is:
bankQuestions.explanation: For WCB = 35° 00', the line lies in quadrant with corresponding reduced angle giving N 35° 00' E.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Remember: Q1: N θ E; Q2: S (180-θ) E; Q3: S (θ-180) W; Q4: N (360-θ) W.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The magnetic bearing of a line is measured as 85° 30'. If the magnetic declination at the observation station is 2° 00' West, what is the true bearing of the line?
bankQuestions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing - Declination West = 85° 30' - 2° 00' = 83° 30'.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Always remember the thumb rule: Add East declination, Subtract West declination.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The magnetic bearing of a line is measured as 96° 30'. If the magnetic declination at the observation station is 3° 00' East, what is the true bearing of the line?
bankQuestions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing + Declination East = 96° 30' + 3° 00' = 99° 30'.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Always remember the thumb rule: Add East declination, Subtract West declination.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning

bankQuestions.question: The magnetic bearing of a line is measured as 107° 30'. If the magnetic declination at the observation station is 4° 00' West, what is the true bearing of the line?
bankQuestions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing - Declination West = 107° 30' - 4° 00' = 103° 30'.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Always remember the thumb rule: Add East declination, Subtract West declination.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The magnetic bearing of a line is measured as 118° 30'. If the magnetic declination at the observation station is 5° 00' East, what is the true bearing of the line?
bankQuestions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing + Declination East = 118° 30' + 5° 00' = 123° 30'.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Always remember the thumb rule: Add East declination, Subtract West declination.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The magnetic bearing of a line is measured as 129° 30'. If the magnetic declination at the observation station is 6° 00' West, what is the true bearing of the line?
bankQuestions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing - Declination West = 129° 30' - 6° 00' = 123° 30'.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Always remember the thumb rule: Add East declination, Subtract West declination.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Town Planning

bankQuestions.question: The magnetic bearing of a line is measured as 140° 30'. If the magnetic declination at the observation station is 2° 00' East, what is the true bearing of the line?
bankQuestions.explanation: True Bearing = Magnetic Bearing + Declination East = 140° 30' + 2° 00' = 142° 30'.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Always remember the thumb rule: Add East declination, Subtract West declination.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Which fundamental principle governs plane table surveying?
options: Parallelism (lines drawn on paper remain parallel to corresponding ground lines)
bankQuestions.explanation: Plane tabling operates on the principle of parallelism: rays and lines plotted on the drawing board remain parallel to the corresponding lines on the ground at each station setup.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Primary principle of plane tabling is Parallelism.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Field observations and map plotting are carried out:
options: After numerical reduction of field books
bankQuestions.explanation: The hallmark of plane table surveying is that sighting, measuring, and plotting are done simultaneously on site, eliminating the need for a separate numerical field book.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plane table: Field work and plotting done simultaneously.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Standard dimensions of a regular plane table drawing board are:
bankQuestions.explanation: A standard plane table board made of well-seasoned teak or pine measures 750 mm × 600 mm (or 600 mm × 600 mm for compact models) with a thickness of 20 mm.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Standard plane table board size = 750 mm × 600 mm.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Technical Education

bankQuestions.question: The beveled working edge of a plane table alidade used for drawing sight rays is termed the:
bankQuestions.explanation: The beveled, graduated, or sloped working edge of the alidade ruler along which sight lines and rays are drawn is called the fiducial edge.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Beveled working edge of alidade = Fiducial edge.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Which accessory is employed to center the plotted station on the drawing paper precisely over the ground station?
bankQuestions.explanation: A plumbing fork (U-frame) carrying a plumb bob is used for centering the plane table, ensuring that the point plotted on the sheet is vertically directly above the ground peg.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plumbing fork with plumb bob = Exact centering in plane table survey.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The primary purpose of a trough compass in plane table surveying is:
options: Orienting the table along the magnetic meridian
bankQuestions.explanation: A trough compass contains a long magnetic needle in a rectangular brass box and is used to establish the Magnetic North and preliminarily orient the plane table.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Trough compass = Aligning / orienting table with magnetic meridian.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Technical Education

bankQuestions.question: The most accurate and reliable method for orienting a plane table at successive stations is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Back-sighting is the most accurate method of orienting a plane table because it is entirely free from local magnetic attractions that can severely distort compass orientation.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Orientation by back-sighting is superior and unaffected by local attraction.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The three successive operations in setting up a plane table at an instrument station are:
options: Fixing on tripod, leveling, and centering & orienting
bankQuestions.explanation: The setup routine consists of: (1) Fixing table on tripod, (2) Leveling the board with a spirit level, and (3) Centering over station peg and orienting parallel to previous stations.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Setup sequence: Leveling -> Centering -> Orientation.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Which method of plane tabling is most suitable for locating inaccessible objects such as distant river banks, hill peaks, or islands?
bankQuestions.explanation: Intersection (graphical triangulation) locates points by intersecting rays drawn from two ends of a measured base line, requiring no chain measurement to the object itself.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Intersection = Inaccessible points / mountainous terrain.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Technical Education

bankQuestions.question: The radiation method of plane tabling is particularly effective when:
options: All details are within easy reach and accessible from a single central station
Points are inaccessible across a wide river
The terrain is dense forest with obstructed lines of sight
The survey extends over a long route of many kilometers
bankQuestions.explanation: Radiation is suitable for small, open areas where all boundary points are accessible and clearly visible from one commanding instrument station.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Radiation = Small, open area accessible from single central station.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The method of plane tabling used for establishing the location of an unknown instrument station by sighting known stations is termed:
bankQuestions.explanation: Resection is the process of determining the plotted position of the station occupied by the plane table by drawing rays to two or more stations whose positions have already been plotted.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Resection = Locating the position of the instrument station itself.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: In the Three-Point Problem of plane tabling, which trial-and-error method is considered the quickest and most accurate in the field?
bankQuestions.explanation: Lehman's method of trial and error is the most rapid, universally adopted, and accurate field method for solving the three-point problem.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Lehman's method = Trial and error method for 3-point problem.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Technical Education

bankQuestions.question: According to Lehman's rules, if the instrument station lies inside the great triangle formed by the three ground stations, the true position 'p' on the sheet will lie:
options: At the centroid of the triangle of error
bankQuestions.explanation: Lehman's Rule 2 states: If the station occupied by the plane table is inside the great triangle ABC, the plotted position 'p' must lie inside the triangle of error.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Inside great triangle -> Point 'p' is INSIDE triangle of error.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: According to Lehman's rules, the perpendicular distance of the true point 'p' from each of the three rays is:
options: Proportional to the distance of the corresponding ground station
Inversely proportional to the station distance
Proportional to the square of the distance
bankQuestions.explanation: Lehman's Rule 3 states: The distance of the true point 'p' from each ray is directly proportional to the distance of the plane table from the respective ground station.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Distance from ray ∝ Ground distance to that station.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The Three-Point Problem becomes completely indeterminate (fails) when the instrument station lies on:
options: The circumference of the circle passing through the three known stations (Great Circle)
The bisector of any interior angle
The straight line joining any two stations
The centroid of the great triangle
bankQuestions.explanation: If the plane table station lies on or near the circle circumscribing the three reference stations (the Great Circle), all rays pass through a common intersection regardless of orientation, making the solution impossible.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: 3-point problem fails if station lies ON the Great Circle (circumscribing circle).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Technical Education

bankQuestions.question: The mechanical method of solving the Three-Point Problem is also known as the:
bankQuestions.explanation: The mechanical method uses tracing paper on which three rays are drawn and shifted over the plan until each ray passes through its respective plotted station.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Mechanical method = Tracing paper method.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Bessel's graphical method for solving the Three-Point Problem is based on the construction of an:
bankQuestions.explanation: Bessel's method is a purely graphical solution based on constructing an inscribed quadrilateral using auxiliary rays.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Bessel's method = Inscribed quadrilateral graphical solution.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: A major source of error in plane tabling that causes the greatest distortion in plotting is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Defective orientation introduces severe angular displacement across the entire map and is by far the most critical observational error in plane tabling.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Defective orientation causes maximum error in plane tabling.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Draftsman Gr. II / Technical Education

bankQuestions.question: In large-scale plane table mapping (e.g., 1:100), an error in centering of 30 cm on the ground results in a plotting error of:
bankQuestions.explanation: Plotting error = Ground error / Scale = 300 mm / 100 = 3 mm. On a 1:100 map, 3 mm is significant, necessitating precise centering.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Error on paper = Ground error / Scale factor.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: A significant operational limitation of plane table surveying is that it:
options: Cannot be conducted during rainy or humid monsoon weather
Cannot determine boundaries of irregular plots
Requires highly expensive electronic computing batteries
bankQuestions.explanation: Plane table surveying uses exposed drawing sheets on site; rain, heavy dew, or high humidity warps and damages the paper, rendering field work impossible.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plane table survey is unsuitable in wet, rainy, or windy climates.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: In plane table surveying, field observations and map plotting are carried out:
options: After numerical reduction of field books
bankQuestions.explanation: The hallmark of plane table surveying is that sighting, measuring, and plotting are done simultaneously on site, eliminating the need for a separate numerical field book.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Plane table: Field work and plotting done simultaneously.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: A curved surface on the earth which is at all points perpendicular to the direction of gravity (plumb line) is called a:
bankQuestions.explanation: A level surface is a curved surface concentric with the mean spheroid of the earth, where every point is perpendicular to the plumb line (gravity vector).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Level surface = Normal to plumb line at all points; Horizontal plane = Tangent to level surface.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The vertical distance of a point above or below an assumed datum surface is called its:
bankQuestions.explanation: The elevation or Reduced Level (RL) of a point is its vertical distance above or below the reference datum surface.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Elevation / RL = Vertical height of point above datum.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: In India, the reference datum for the Great Trigonometrical Survey (GTS) is Mean Sea Level (MSL) established at:
bankQuestions.explanation: GTS datum for all levelling in India is the Mean Sea Level determined by continuous tidal observations at Mumbai (formerly Bombay).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Indian GTS Datum = Mean Sea Level at Mumbai.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: The first staff reading taken after setting up a level at any instrument station is always a:
bankQuestions.explanation: A Back Sight (BS) is always the first sight taken after setting up the instrument, directed to a point of known elevation (Bench Mark or Change Point).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Back Sight (BS) = First sight taken on known RL point.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The last staff reading taken before moving a level to a new position is termed:
bankQuestions.explanation: A Fore Sight (FS) is the final sight taken on a point prior to picking up the instrument, signifying the conclusion of that instrument setup.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Fore Sight (FS) = Last staff reading from an instrument setup.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: A point on which both a Fore Sight and a Back Sight are observed to advance the line of levels is called a:
bankQuestions.explanation: A Change Point (CP) or Turning Point (TP) is a stable ground point on which a Fore Sight is read from the old station and a Back Sight is read from the new station.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Change Point = Both FS and BS taken on same point.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: In the Height of Instrument (Collimation) method of levelling, the Height of Instrument (HI) is computed as:
options: RL of Bench Mark + Back Sight (BS)
RL of Bench Mark - Back Sight (BS)
RL of Bench Mark + Fore Sight (FS)
RL of Bench Mark / Back Sight (BS)
bankQuestions.explanation: Height of Instrument (HI) = RL of Bench Mark + Back Sight (BS). The RL of any succeeding point = HI - (IS or FS).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: HI = RL + BS; RL = HI - Staff Reading.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Which arithmetical check applies to the Rise and Fall method of levelling?
bankQuestions.explanation: In the Rise and Fall method, the three-fold check is: ∑BS - ∑FS = ∑Rise - ∑Fall = Last RL - First RL. This provides a complete check on intermediate sights as well.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Rise & Fall check: ∑BS - ∑FS = ∑Rise - ∑Fall = Last RL - First RL.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The correction for earth's curvature for a sight distance of 'd' kilometres is given by:
bankQuestions.explanation: The curvature of the earth causes the level line to drop below the horizontal line of collimation by Cc = d² / (2R) = 0.0785 d² m, which is always subtractive (-).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Curvature correction = - 0.0785 d² m (Always subtractive).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: Atmospheric refraction causes the line of sight to bend towards the earth, resulting in a refraction correction of:
bankQuestions.explanation: Refraction bends the ray downward, making staff readings appear smaller than actual. Correction Cr = + (1/7) Cc ≈ + 0.0112 d² m, which is additive (+).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Refraction correction Cr = + 0.0112 d² m (Additive, 1/7 of curvature).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The combined correction for curvature and refraction for a sight distance of 'd' km is:
bankQuestions.explanation: Combined correction C = Cc + Cr = - 0.0785 d² + 0.0112 d² = - 0.0673 d² metres.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Combined correction = - 0.0673 d² m (subtractive).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Reciprocal levelling eliminates the errors caused by:
options: Curvature, refraction, and collimation error simultaneously
bankQuestions.explanation: By balancing readings taken reciprocally across wide rivers or ravines from both banks, reciprocal levelling completely cancels out curvature, atmospheric refraction, and collimation errors.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Reciprocal levelling cancels curvature, refraction, and collimation errors.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: When taking a staff reading on the underside of a bridge girder or roof ceiling (inverted staff), the RL of the point is calculated as:
bankQuestions.explanation: For an inverted staff, the staff reading is negative (-). Elevation = HI - (- Staff Reading) = HI + Staff Reading.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Inverted staff: RL = HI + Staff Reading (staff reading is treated as negative).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: The sensitivity of a spirit bubble tube increases with:
options: An increase in the radius of curvature of the internal tube surface
An increase in the viscosity of the bubble liquid
A decrease in the length of the bubble
A smaller diameter of the glass tube
bankQuestions.explanation: Bubble sensitivity increases with a larger radius of curvature (R), longer bubble length, larger tube diameter, smoother glass finish, and lower liquid viscosity.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Sensitivity increases with larger radius of curvature and lower liquid viscosity.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: The vertical distance between two consecutive contour lines on a topographic map is known as:
bankQuestions.explanation: The vertical distance between two successive contour lines is called the contour interval. It is kept constant throughout a given map.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Contour interval = Vertical distance; Horizontal equivalent = Horizontal distance.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: Concentric closed contour lines with higher elevation values inside indicate a:
bankQuestions.explanation: Concentric closed contour loops with elevations increasing progressively toward the center represent a hill peak or mountain summit.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Values increase inward = Hill; Values decrease inward = Depression/Pond.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Concentric closed contour lines with lower elevation values toward the inside represent a:
bankQuestions.explanation: Concentric contours whose values decrease toward the center signify a depression, pond, lake basin, or crater.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Values decrease inward = Depression / Pond.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.question: Contour lines can unite to form a single continuous line only in the case of a:
bankQuestions.explanation: Contour lines of different elevations coalesce into a single line only where the terrain is a strictly vertical cliff wall.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Contours unite = Vertical cliff; Contours cross each other = Overhanging cliff.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Overseer Gr. III (LSGD / PWD)

bankQuestions.question: Contour lines can cross each other only in the exceptional case of an:
bankQuestions.explanation: Contours cross each other only in the case of an overhanging cliff or an underground cavern/cave.
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Contours cross = Overhanging cliff or cave.
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Surveyor Gr. II (Survey & Land Records)

bankQuestions.question: Contour lines cross ridge and valley lines at an angle of:
bankQuestions.explanation: Because water flows down the steepest path perpendicular to contours, drainage valley lines and watershed ridge lines always cross contour lines at right angles (90°).
bankQuestions.rankerTip: Contours cross ridge and valley lines at right angles (90°).
bankQuestions.examName: Kerala PSC Tracer / Overseer (Kerala Water Authority)

bankQuestions.rankerTip: HI = RL + BS; Target RL = HI - FS.
